We’ve got just one week left until the February 2nd voter registration deadline, and we need to make sure every eligible Texan who wants to vote in the March primary has the chance to get registered.
It won’t surprise you to know that Texas doesn’t make this easy. No same-day voter registration. No automatic registration. No online registration. We don’t have the luxury of waiting or hoping people figure it out in time. If Texans want to vote in the March primary, they need to get registered now.
That’s why Powered by People is out there every single day. Meeting folks where they are—in neighborhoods, on campuses, at community events. Having real conversations. And helping get Texans registered so they don’t miss this deadline.
We’ve seen this work time and time again. Every conversation matters. Every form matters. Every person we help register strengthens our democracy and brings us closer to a Texas where everyone has a say—on education, health care, the minimum wage, and the future we want for generations to come.

| | Patriot,
---
| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn't a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal -- the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God's grace. **

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." **_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=cf5be0fc70fd4be9a9a734f4b8c1d7ea&_e=apdINwWYw-5e2VeQN5WCBSGxrK6lb5g42SBfPGIB82lqEZyIAJueY1jIHBT-_Fq_DWOgkNhis9ySc-l9iSSo_aPtjP_LvIqKY-m4lm04IugwYbL2FAGft6HoPI1WuO2wFL7EMemUMahIKyXegdczmXimmuM0la6YCEf-xetXOBNmaO4RTXU0yv8WKpLbIGnqo8jcAAZy-jUCdDjqQlaREhCbIbbpN8IAvoePxkKJ0BQF2lPzECFnoUurIZM0B4urc_BptZ1bu-ed431A_8ly0phT3yVreMZPXHg6l39RqIS_eEUSX0SIIEYHo5ZXzs7oqAOdGDfTrOq9qJ8v7Uh_FCNbyzyZV9_gQu_2SeclaMBC1nrJ8-MLvXlzsB--n0KNF2odf-sk_MTJ46WZa-Dmjhhv3E4xVB-5BFMvarENfa1oXKm-nRCVrkO9y_hfMKVbEv2wdSY5CtKv-LB1uIlWdLvFJKS9QQ3myDCp4Ncc_SuUZSlyCvmoLX7YwnwbJfn4FEWfTRBa84bHgcXohKPM7F8SYBBHLdjKZjNJY-8JqVIpQiS4tkzejqlp8nuaIcW-UIxCfBov1Y7RUdyw15yQs9TDW5-oMimHIo27E0RVNe9F77BtAdk77qGJZFeit7eGqPNliMkv9iNQ2cugJ10CnU3SRxnemNNIYqbSR1J_ILodXbcain4rJ-gxb1Lw75m1)
---
When you read it, you will hear Charlie's voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie's hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

| Peter,

I am furious about what I am seeing and hearing out of ICE in Maryland.

Over the past several months, I’ve heard from thousands who are terrified for their families and neighbors. I can’t sit by and watch the abuses coming out of Minneapolis or the reports of American citizens being unlawfully detained, denied basic access to medical care, food, and legal counsel and illegally deported right here in Maryland.

That is why I am demanding to inspect the ICE detention facility in Baltimore and meet directly with detainees and staff. As a Member of Congress, I have a constitutional duty to conduct oversight, and ICE has a legal obligation to cooperate.

Let me be clear. The real domestic threats are not coming from immigrant families or peaceful communities. They are coming from the White House.

Donald Trump and Kristi Noem have weaponized immigration enforcement and stripped it of guardrails. The result is fear, abuse, and a system that operates in the shadows. I refuse to accept that as normal. **_That is why I am demanding that Noem resign from DHS._**

I will be inspecting conditions, demanding records, and pressing ICE to explain how it is operating in our communities. _**Marylanders deserve the truth, and ICE deserves accountability.**_

# Visalia and Tulare Police Officers’ Associations Endorse Magsig for Senate
---
|
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** January 26th, 2026Contact: nathan@nathanmagsig.com
---
| | | | | | **(Clovis, CA)** \- Today, Nathan Magsig announced the endorsements of the Visalia Police Officers Association and the Tulare Police Officers Association for his run for State Senate.
Magsig expressed his appreciation for the endorsements, stating:
_“It’s an honor to receive the support of the dedicated officers who serve the communities of Visalia and Tulare. Throughout my service at the local level, I’ve worked to ensure our law enforcement professionals have the resources, training, and respect they deserve, and I will continue that commitment as State Senator.”_
The endorsements from the Visalia and Tulare Police Officers Associations add to Magsig’s growing support from public safety organizations across the Valley, underscoring that he is law enforcement’s clear choice for State Senate.
View the full list of endorsements [HERE](https://nathanmagsig.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=566959e132b9980afc6311201&id=6474afd1a3&e=6cdbd718cb)
---
| | ###
Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor, former Mayor of Clovis, and is running for the 12th Senate District. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

name: Brianna For Colorado
subject: Special Edition Newsletter--Statement on Recent ICE Murders & How to Help
body:
| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/e16a78b41aaf/special-edition-newsletter-statement-on-recent-ice-murders-how-to-help?e=8249791cac)
---
| | | | [|
---](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=734099a21a&e=8249791cac)
| | | | | | | | | | | | Hi everyone. This special edition newsletter will be all about ICE. I will discuss how to report activity, how to support, and other ways you can help.
I first want to take a moment to discuss the recent atrocities committed by ICE and honor those affected. [On January 7th, Renée Good was murdered by ICE agents in Minneapolis, Minnesota](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=d4757dc052&e=8249791cac). Good and her wife were in their car working to notify their neighbors of ICE’s activity and be a witness if anything occurred. Good was approached by ICE agents and was told conflicting commands: to get out of her car and to drive away. During the confusion, Agent Jonathan Ross pulled out his gun and fired three shots into their car, killing Good.
[On January 24th, Alex Pretti was also murdered by ICE agents in Minneapolis, Minnesota](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=17ce6eb9b4&e=8249791cac). Pretti was attending a peaceful protest in Minneapolis when he saw a woman be shoved by agents. Pretti, an ICU nurse at the VA, stepped in to protect the woman and re-direct the agents. The agents pepper-sprayed Pretti, pinned him to the ground, hit him with their guns, and subsequently shot him in the back murdering him. While Pretti was legally carrying a concealed handgun, he did not pull it out once and was instead recording the altercation with his cell phone. The ICE agents had already disarmed him before they shot him.
I want to make it clear that Good and Pretti are [not the first victims of ICE](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=57ffb2ea37&e=8249791cac) and they definitely will not be the last. Additionally, there is lots of conflicting information out there on their murders. The Minnesota Department of Corrections has created a [website](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=90acf2424e&e=8249791cac) to combat the blatant misinformation the federal government is putting out.
Both Good and Pretti deserve justice and a fair investigation, not one done by the agency who murdered them or any other Trump influenced agency. These shootings must be investigated by state and local authorities. I ask you to contact our US Senators, [Senator Hickenlooper](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=f7320a34a7&e=8249791cac) and [Senator Bennet](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=770c0caa52&e=8249791cac), to advocate for actions at the federal level. My thoughts are with Minnesota.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Like many people, I am scared. I am scared that I no longer recognize the country I love. I am scared that the system of government—that I myself I am part of—no longer has the checks and balances its’ supposed to. I am scared that I have no idea what the future holds or how to ensure my family and constituents are safe.
I will never waiver to these injustices and will fight to uphold the Constitution. We must have hope and support our community. I will support any legislation that comes forward to protect Coloradans and stop ICE. I will remain outspoken of the need to hold ICE accountable. I condemn any legislator who does not take a position and stand up for their constituents. I have always run on transparency and accountability, and that still holds true now, more than ever.
The state legislature has introduced bills like [SB26-](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=1eac8f37f8&e=8249791cac)[005](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=be04858252&e=8249791cac), which allows individuals to hold federal officials accountable in court. We are also working to eliminate the mask-wearing of federal agents. In the past, we have also focused on bills to increase the training for law enforcement, and strengthen Civil Rights for immigrants in our communities. Colorado Democrats are currently finalizing another package of bills to combat ICE and protect Coloradans. It will be publicly announced next week.
---
|
---
| |
# [REPORT ICE ACTIVITY]()
---
| |
The [Constitution’s 4th Amendment protects everyone](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=ba5571ed19&e=8249791cac) who is in the US. This [link from the ACLU](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=2cf87e2144&e=8249791cac) will help you understand your rights if you are stopped by ICE. Here’s[ ](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=0a3dfc9b4b&e=8249791cac)[an article with more contex](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=13c9f4e841&e=8249791cac)[t](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=2cdf696442&e=8249791cac). **If you witness ICE activity or need to document an experience, you can contact the Colorado Rapid Response Network / Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition hotline (bilingual, 24/7): 844-864-8341** [KEEP THIS LINK](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=01d7b342f8&e=8249791cac) for ways to connect people to legal support, documentation resources, and community response efforts. I recommend saving it on your phone’s home screen for easy access in an emergency. Equally important, you can check rumors against the work of [Colorado Rapid Response Network’s (CORRN)](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=c1593430d6&e=8249791cac) trained confirmers to avoid spreading fear unnecessarily - if you see social media posts about ICE presence, check CORRN and let people know if a rumor or report was already investigated by CORRN.If you would like to be more deeply involved, CORRN holds regular trainings for confirmers, dispatchers, and other roles. They may be overwhelmed with interest at the moment. However, you can sign up for their [list](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=bf3a438c17&e=8249791cac) to be notified of any upcoming event. Spanish speakers and donations are particularly needed at this moment.[We Keep Us Safe (CO)](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=7817378245&e=8249791cac) has a website packed with information on ICE and how best to take action to protect neighbors.
---
| |
# [MUTUAL AID & COMMUNITY SUPPORT]()
---
| | [Stand with Minnesota](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=ed57828cf9&e=8249791cac) has a database for reputable, grassroots organizations that you can support to help those in Minnesota.
[Mutual Aid Monday](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=9a3a088aca&e=8249791cac) is a Denver grassroots organization specifically focused on mutual aid and supporting the community.The [Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=1335186161&e=8249791cac), in partnership with many other community groups, is organizing periodic canvassing to make sure neighbors know their rights and know where to turn for help.[The American Friends Service Committee](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=139025cb5e&e=8249791cac) organizes teams of allies to support the work of CORRN and immigrants in Denver. Their website has resources for families to create safety plans and complete legal paperwork to be prepared if a family member is detained.[RMIAN](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=595c600ccf&e=8249791cac) and the [Denver Immigrant Legal Services Fund](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=8f2ecd6820&e=8249791cac) are overwhelmed with the need for legal representation; they are excellent places to donate if you can afford to or to volunteer if you are a lawyer or Spanish speaker. [Immigrant Freedom Fund](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=89b51c4c96&e=8249791cac) pays bond for those in detention at the Aurora GEO facility who cannot afford to pay themselves.[Casa de Paz](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=02926ebc0f&e=8249791cac) welcomes people who are released from immigration detention and supports people while they are detained.
[Movimiento Poder](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=da297fe6b6&e=8249791cac) cultivates the leadership of immigrant youth and their parents in Denver and leads family safety trainings. Support their grassroots work and their members by [donating](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=23c02ed06e&e=8249791cac), look to their website for family and school safety resources, and reach out if you know a school/group where a training would be welcome.
---
| |
# [OTHER WAYS TO HELP]()
---
| |
Finally, here are a couple other things you can do every day to support our community:
* Share verified hotline and “know your rights” resources - the[ ](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=366b4d6879&e=8249791cac)[ACLU has some great information](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=6f9e08a604&e=8249791cac) you can keep handy. If you can afford to, [buy red cards](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=558265f682&e=8249791cac) and donate them to canvassers.

* Support immigrant-owned small businesses who need reliable income more than ever as their communities are under tremendous stress - and consider [boycotting ICE profiteers](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=fca09bbe0f&e=8249791cac). East Colfax is a hub for immigrant entrepreneurs and the East Colfax Community Collective has a [directory](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=754cf6b39c&e=8249791cac) of small businesses on the corridor (they also support their members, both residents and businesses, in all kinds of ways and are a great place to donate).

* Learn how to document or serve as a trained observer safely. [We Keep Us Safe](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=4358db9403&e=8249791cac) is a good hub for learning resources and training opportunities

---
|
---
| | Finally, please know that my door and inbox are always open, even if you do not live in my district. As I said earlier, I believe a system of support and community is one of the most vital things to have right now. You are always welcome to contact me.
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| | [**Virtual Office Hours**]()**** 💻
---

[**Sign up here**](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=ae0a36e088&e=8249791cac)**on Calendly!**

Equally important, you can check rumors against the work of trained confirmers to avoid spreading fear unnecessarily - if you see social media posts about ICE presence, check CORRN and let people know if a rumor or report was already investigated by CORRN.If you would like to be more deeply involved, CORRN holds regular trainings for confirmers, dispatchers, and other roles. They may be overwhelmed with interest at the moment. However, you can sign up for their to be notified of any upcoming event. Spanish speakers and donations are particularly needed at this moment. has a website packed with information on ICE and how best to take action to protect neighbors. | | [MUTUAL AID & COMMUNITY SUPPORT]() | | has a database for reputable, grassroots organizations that you can support to help those in Minnesota. is a Denver grassroots organization specifically focused on mutual aid and supporting the community.The , in partnership with many other community groups, is organizing periodic canvassing to make sure neighbors know their rights and know where to turn for help. organizes teams of allies to support the work of CORRN and immigrants in Denver. Their website has resources for families to create safety plans and complete legal paperwork to be prepared if a family member is detained. and the are overwhelmed with the need for legal representation; they are excellent places to donate if you can afford to or to volunteer if you are a lawyer or Spanish speaker. pays bond for those in detention at the Aurora GEO facility who cannot afford to pay themselves. welcomes people who are released from immigration detention and supports people while they are detained. cultivates the leadership of immigrant youth and their parents in Denver and leads family safety trainings. Support their grassroots work and their members by , look to their website for family and school safety resources, and reach out if you know a school/group where a training would be welcome. | | [OTHER WAYS TO HELP]() | | Finally, here are a couple other things you can do every day to support our community: Share verified hotline and “know your rights” resources - the you can keep handy. If you can afford to, and donate them to canvassers. Support immigrant-owned small businesses who need reliable income more than ever as their communities are under tremendous stress - and consider . East Colfax is a hub for immigrant entrepreneurs and the East Colfax Community Collective has a of small businesses on the corridor (they also support their members, both residents and businesses, in all kinds of ways and are a great place to donate). Learn how to document or serve as a trained observer safely. is a good hub for learning resources and training opportunities | | | Finally, please know that my door and inbox are always open, even if you do not live in my district. As I said earlier, I believe a system of support and community is one of the most vital things to have right now. name: Ilhan Omar
subject: Alex Pretti
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260126-1869-foote&t=1001&akid=1869%2E342411%2E7fYd5u ]Squad Victory Fund

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/signup/abolish-ice-jan-2026/?source=em20260126-1869&t=1002&akid=1869%2E342411%2E7fYd5u ]Alex Pretti

Peter — One of my
constituents, Alex Pretti, was murdered in cold blood by immigration
agents in the streets of Minneapolis on Saturday.

Alex was a 37-year-old ICU nurse who worked for the Veterans
Administration. His job was to take care of those who had served our
country when they were sick and injured. His family and friends say he was
a kind soul who enjoyed hiking and camping.

When George Floyd was murdered by police in Alex’s own neighborhood in
2020, he joined the local protests and stood in solidarity with his
community. Alex did the same when Renee Good was murdered just weeks ago
by ICE. He is one of hundreds of thousands of Minnesotans who have
protested, documented, and resisted ICE’s campaign of terror over the last
month.

Alex’s final act before being killed was to help a woman who was being
beaten by immigration agents on the side of the road. Alex was swarmed by
a team of agents, pepper-sprayed, wrestled to the ground, and shot several
times.

Peter — I have
seen the video from every angle. Many of you have by now. There is no
earthly justification for an immigration officer to take this man’s life.
This was a state-sanctioned murder, and blood is on the hands of Trump and
his entire fascist administration.

But, as if this incident couldn’t be even more horrifying, the
administration is doubling down on lies, slander, and defamation against
an innocent man who was slain by his own government rather than facing
accountability.

Kristi Noem did not miss a beat in labeling Alex a “domestic terrorist”,
just like she did to Renee Good. Border Patrol commander Greg Bovino
rushed to falsely claim that Alex intended to do “maximum damage and
massacre law enforcement.” Stephen Miller referred to Alex as “an
assassin” who “tried to murder federal agents,” and Vice President JD
Vance boosted it.

This is unadulterated bullsh*t – unbelievable propaganda to cover their
behinds after yet another innocent person was murdered under their watch.

Alex’s family responded in a statement, "The sickening lies told about our
son by the administration are reprehensible and disgusting... Please get the
truth out about our son. He was a good man.”

Peter, the
murder of Alex Pretti is not an isolated incident. Simply put, the
occupation of Minneapolis is an unprecedented crisis for our Constitution,
our democracy, and our entire way of life.

Americans gunned down without accountability. Hundreds beaten and
brutalized, from the elderly to tiny babies. Civil rights torn to shreds
as ICE breaks down doors, rams into cars, and smashes windows. Citizens
arrested without due process and dumped on the side of the road. Families
were separated at gunpoint, and toddlers were kidnapped to use as bait
against their parents. The situation has reached a boiling point, and it’s
time for it to end for the sake of all that is good and decent.

We must get ICE and DHS out of Minnesota, strip them of their funding,
impeach Kristi Noem for her catastrophic failure of leadership, charge ICE
killers and thugs for murder and assault, and organize to punish
Republicans at the ballot box this November for their steadfast reign of
terror.

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

One more thing,
Peter:

Trump’s immigration regime is out-of-control, unaccountable, and a clear
danger to our communities. We are calling on Congress to stand tall in
defense of our Constitution and block any and all funding for DHS and
ICE. Please, [ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/signup/abolish-ice-jan-2026/?source=em20260126-1869&t=1003&akid=1869%2E342411%2E7fYd5u ]add your name to our petition and help us show a massive
wave of resistance to the violence and civil rights abuses we are seeing
in Minnesota and across the country:

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/signup/abolish-ice-jan-2026/?source=em20260126-1869&t=1004&akid=1869%2E342411%2E7fYd5u ]SIGN ON NOW

name: Dan Freeman (via Democrats.org)
subject: Legal update after this weekend:
body:
---
Hi Derek, this is Dan Freeman, the DNC’s Litigation Director. On Saturday, a federal immigration agent shot and killed Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. For the past three days, millions of Americans have watched eyewitness footage of the events and seen an American citizen assaulted by federal agents, driven to his knees, and then shot repeatedly. President Trump and his administration are trying to convince the public that Pretti posed a threat to agents’ safety. Alex Pretti was an ICU nurse for the Veterans Administration. He was a helper and an everyday hero. The administration's repeated lies about his killing are at once horrifying and ludicrous. In the aftermath of this tragedy, Attorney General Pam Bondi sent a letter to Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, tying the “chaos in Minnesota” to the state’s refusal to provide sensitive personal information about Minnesota voters to the federal government. The Justice Department is demanding driver’s license numbers, Social Security numbers, and voting history, as they collect information on every voter in the country. **Derek, let me be clear. Neither this request nor the end goal of creating a national voter database is legal, and the Democratic National Committee won’t stand for it.** We have already filed briefs in five states fighting back against unlawful demands for state voter rolls, with more to come this week. We’ve also sent letters warning ten Republican-led states negotiating agreements with the Department of Justice — to provide voter files and purge voters when the DOJ tells them to — that these actions would violate federal law. And earlier today, I appeared in federal court in Oregon, where a judge had ordered the Justice Department to explain the relevance of Attorney General Bondi’s letter to voter file requests around the country. We had already defeated President Trump’s attempt to get California’s unredacted voter file in federal court, and today the federal court in Oregon handed President Trump another defeat by dismissing the voter file demand. President Trump, Attorney General Bondi, Customs and Border Protection Commander-at-Large Greg Bovino, and other members of the administration are demanding compliance from American citizens, in the streets and in the polling booth. Our response is simple: **We’re not afraid of you, and we’ll see you in court.** Thank you for taking the time to read this email, and thank you for caring so deeply about our country. Dan Dan Freeman
Litigation Director
Democratic National Committee

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

Donald Trump’s Department of Justice is more focused on investigating my office than the killing of Renee Good.
| Team,

I’m suing the Department of Homeland Security to stop their dangerous, illegal, and unconstitutional operation in Minnesota.

Thousands of armed, masked, and poorly trained federal agents are terrorizing the Twin Cities. They’ve brazenly and repeatedly used excessive force against Minnesotans, arrested and threatened innocent bystanders, and conducted militarized raids in schools, churches, hospitals, and other sensitive locations.

This violates the law, the First and Tenth Amendment, and the Constitution’s guarantee of equal sovereignty.

No one should be stopped, questioned, or targeted by ICE solely because of how they look, how they speak, or where they come from. No parent should have to wonder if their child will come home safely from school. And no business should have to shut its doors due to fears of violence.

**As Attorney General, I’m doing everything in my power to stop this federal invasion and protect Minnesotans from harm.**

name: Deb Haaland
subject: Enough is enough
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=7107%2E400544%2EZvzPGD)
---
Friend, my heart is heavy.

On Saturday, while Minnesotans and many across the country stood against the disgusting and terrifying violence ICE is carrying out in our country, federal agents shot and killed another person. He was not the first person unjustly killed by ICE, and most likely, he will not be the last, and I know that’s why so many people are angry. I’m angry too.

I don't have the words to express my horror at what is happening in our country right now, but I do know that we must continue to fight back — in any way we can. Resistance can be organizing a protest, delivering coffee and providing a warm place for protestors, or calling your lawmakers or running for local office. Hope is only lost when resistance stops, and there is power in our voices and collective action.
**New Mexicans are not strangers to adversity. In fact, we are strong and support each other. To New Mexicans who are living in fear, worrying about loved ones, and watching what is happening in our communities with horror, I want you to know I stand with you in this fight — I always have and I always will. Today, as your neighbor and friend. Next year, as your governor.
**
While state and local law enforcement work hard to protect our communities, under-trained ICE agents are using violence, rounding people up, tearing families apart, targeting Black and brown communities, and breaking the law. And now, Americans are being killed in the streets for standing up, speaking out, and opposing them.
**This is unacceptable. Our communities are _less safe_ as a direct result of Donald Trump's policies. It's un-American, and it must stop.**
If Donald Trump and ICE want to bring the violence and unrest to New Mexico, they will have to get through my administration and me. We will have zero tolerance for their injustice, and we will use every authority at our disposal to stop them.
I will do everything in my power to protect our public spaces — like schools, churches, courthouses, healthcare centers, and state government facilities.
I will support efforts to require ICE agents to identify themselves and remove their masks and to ban ICE detention centers in our state.
Governors are the last line of defense when the federal government abuses its resources and undermines civil liberties. Our responsibility is to protect families, safeguard our communities, and make sure no one lives in fear. You have my promise: I will hold Donald Trump accountable and protect New Mexicans. Always.
This isn't over. I expect it will get harder before it gets easier. But together, we will defend our rights and liberties.
With you in this fight,

Deb
|

| | Friends,
At a recent [Attorney General debate](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fUECDkzZOfCL8GEkqfuQsk70PVaO-d0rwrZK7IZVkC_pHzf48QxStncUOhb77F_AwX4WCNBco4edSW8P2M2a9X38KD32kuH_TbbqkPLLUCyiRZvQaDoKia-rM3NjWoiWg8jyHTBn174hvbF2owQGF7dlp-kLi3zJaL3OesLRHdUCX-DlR02sW-NcfHvJVEVq&c=wgHMyzWq_AN2JP_pt46-yomnUzQDS5Lo9kTaRajKMoIVI-jK471YDg==&ch=W2eYA3e6AY_-0e58pg6JrVKPI4489W3XU3hIz8yKWLKr8GaHR6KiBg==) hosted by the North Oakland Republican Club, we were asked an important question: Would you sue to stop sanctuary cities?

Here is my answer:
[Doug Lloyd on Sanctuary Cities](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fUECDkzZOfCL8GEkqfuQsk70PVaO-d0rwrZK7IZVkC_pHzf48QxStncUOhb77F_AHJ5Ax9BRJGG2YZ-tJxAqpDhXZIWJ5enHBzXzx9eZ5LRE1Yz0DgSFVifdNdhIELPa8-F1fjtxPPDBUskrDEae624q4SvMbJBSfqwD9FMDrPn1x5S5Hw1A1FmUPmOH3ktu4_94Jcun7x0oOpvO74oFPA==&c=wgHMyzWq_AN2JP_pt46-yomnUzQDS5Lo9kTaRajKMoIVI-jK471YDg==&ch=W2eYA3e6AY_-0e58pg6JrVKPI4489W3XU3hIz8yKWLKr8GaHR6KiBg==)
My opponent answered first and said that if elected Attorney General, he would use his power to sue any sanctuary city. That approach mirrors what we see from our current Attorney General and Democrat leadership who regularly disregard local control and use lawsuits as political weapons.
That answer may sound tough, but it ignores how the Constitution and the law actually work.
Here is the truth.
Cities are creatures of the state, and the state can only sue them if they violate a state law. There is nothing in the Michigan Constitution or in any statute that bans or prohibits sanctuary policies. Republican legislators, including Aric Nesbitt, have tried to pass legislation to change that, but those efforts were blocked by Democrat leadership.
Because no such law exists, sanctuary city policies are not illegal in Michigan. Filing lawsuits with no legal basis would get thrown out of court, waste taxpayer dollars, and embarrass the Attorney General's office.
Thankfully, there is a lawful and effective way forward.
Republicans are united in opposing sanctuary cities. The real solution is electing Republicans who can win and pass legislation that becomes law.
In the meantime, the Attorney General should work with Republican leadership in the House and Senate to cut state funding to sanctuary cities. President Trump has announced this approach at the federal level, and Michigan should follow suit. With a Republican Senate and governor, we can then pass legislation banning sanctuary city policies statewide.
Once funding is addressed, the Attorney General should coordinate with the federal government to form a joint task force. This would allow the Michigan State Police and the Attorney General's office to work directly with federal authorities to prosecute criminals shielded by these policies.
The Attorney General must also respect local control. We have seen the damage done when Democrats strip local control and force unwanted policies on our communities. Republicans cannot become activist hypocrites who play the same political games.
Michigan needs a serious leader who tells the truth, not someone who says whatever sounds good in a debate.
As Attorney General, I will protect all citizens, uphold the law, and deliver real results. I will not mislead voters or play political games.

clean_body: The Lawful Path Forward | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, At a recent == hosted by the North Oakland Republican Club, we were asked an important question: Would you sue to stop sanctuary cities? Here is my answer: == My opponent answered first and said that if elected Attorney General, he would use his power to sue any sanctuary city. That approach mirrors what we see from our current Attorney General and Democrat leadership who regularly disregard local control and use lawsuits as political weapons. That answer may sound tough, but it ignores how the Constitution and the law actually work. Here is the truth. Cities are creatures of the state, and the state can only sue them if they violate a state law. There is nothing in the Michigan Constitution or in any statute that bans or prohibits sanctuary policies. Republican legislators, including Aric Nesbitt, have tried to pass legislation to change that, but those efforts were blocked by Democrat leadership. Because no such law exists, sanctuary city policies are not illegal in Michigan. Filing lawsuits with no legal basis would get thrown out of court, waste taxpayer dollars, and embarrass the Attorney General's office. Thankfully, there is a lawful and effective way forward. Republicans are united in opposing sanctuary cities. The real solution is electing Republicans who can win and pass legislation that becomes law. In the meantime, the Attorney General should work with Republican leadership in the House and Senate to cut state funding to sanctuary cities. President Trump has announced this approach at the federal level, and Michigan should follow suit. With a Republican Senate and governor, we can then pass legislation banning sanctuary city policies statewide. Once funding is addressed, the Attorney General should coordinate with the federal government to form a joint task force. This would allow the Michigan State Police and the Attorney General's office to work directly with federal authorities to prosecute criminals shielded by these policies. The Attorney General must also respect local control. We have seen the damage done when Democrats strip local control and force unwanted policies on our communities. Republicans cannot become activist hypocrites who play the same political games. Michigan needs a serious leader who tells the truth, not someone who says whatever sounds good in a debate. As Attorney General, I will protect all citizens, uphold the law, and deliver real results. I will not mislead voters or play political games. ## Trump Sends Border Czar to Minnesota
President Trump announced Monday he is sending White House border czar [Tom Homan to Minnesota](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu4zAQBNCvkToKJCVLVsHiGnW-9kqBJpfWHkiuQG6sOF8fKAHyA6kHGMybf7f1ZjFifvy1CQwHWjMcNQIzlPVOxUNxH7YwJcwZKrF9UPSrlnoUUgk9rd5ifK1D600A0NC3YNQ0zhelrvPcbkYGB1fbz3ZW6u4GCNaNTloNIMdh8r5Fc7ZJpSel5HCZut6H6xRkkErKSxhCM0jwyFS6_4SZNwjxRU8onaPURrMx77Xp_zR6afRyHEcX6P1UnHmjl50iMrra6IXLW9qFhz3Sq4pvnjh9gimJjZLN4gcq0IGgHYplpFxFsA7EEylCZuE2S7Utxu8Hxoh1nJpBPpLF-LWKf3Xl0-jPAAAA___kII1R) to manage immigration enforcement operations following a fatal shooting of a protester this weekend. The president wrote that Homan is "[tough but fair, and will report directly to me](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u8yAUxvGrMVuiA-bDDAyv9MpbOlXqaFE4xFTYWHCSKL36Kr2Frs8j_Yb_x2W5-Fzyfn3zGzpKddnx0QsSYVs-a4vYwrdvVLe879gr-WstcREg9An4SZgl-lyei2TRJUSBI0PHjbaK88latjoDXk5TMMHGMaHxNsagtEkQ0CsTLcvupQEXhnOQypzHmCaTIAEHUEmmQQLGTLWdv2reacVUnvWO7RzqxopbiY4-jP8GMQ9ipnajtdeQfXn9r1FCQ1_-192X-N5u2zGI-aid-iBmzpXVXEujQI3aGjWy5uLxyKXkrs0g4br5_Esx-lOfuxM_AQAA__8gT3hK)." What are the fundamental principles we are governed by and expected to live by?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f30164ae-be58-4698-80ce-074311748c1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Because when you lose clarity on that, everything else collapses into confusion. Personal life. Home life. Civil engagement. Without a moral compass, you do not know where to go.
That is why I keep coming back to the Bill of Rights. The founders wrote constraints into the Constitution to govern how we interact with each other and what kind of state we live in. When you boil it down through all the nonsense, all the points of view, all the slants and twists, the outline is fundamental, clear, and true.
And right now, we are losing that clarity.
**Narratives Are Winning Because Truth Is Getting Rebuilt**
I am watching people obsess over individual incidents and treat them like the whole story. Zooming in on videos. Rewinding. Picking apart frames like it is courtroom evidence.
At the same time, I am already seeing AI reconstruct those same videos in different ways, packaged for propaganda and political slants.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5a0388d6-5d50-4b18-99e6-15176f9ecf4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you let your beliefs be built from isolated clips, and those clips can be rebuilt by for an agenda to match whatever story someone wants to sell, you are not thinking anymore. You are being guided.
The answer is not to pretend the slants do not exist. The answer is to anchor back to the founding principles of what governs us and how we want to be governed.
### We Are Losing Our Way
I have been saying for a long time that we have been losing our way. Political slants and jockeying have made us more confused, not more informed.
I believe the Bill of Rights is deep-seated in the consciousness of Americans, so much so that many people think it is universal truth. As if it is not specific to one nation.
But it is.
It is universal for us, but not for other nations. That is part of what gives this country strength. It creates a unique individual sense of identity and governing rules that are supposed to be unbendable.
But they are being bent.
And when those rules become flexible, the idea of what it means to be American becomes hazy. It becomes a costume instead of a civic identity and responsibility.
### Rights Are Not Always Convenient, and That Is the Point
We have to get back to understanding that these rules will not always serve your political purpose in the moment. They will be uncomfortable. They will hurt some people and benefit others at certain times.
They are a building block that everyone has chosen to participate in. I emphasize chosen because I have said before why I criticize America. I criticize it because I choose to live here. That choice is conscious. It comes with obligations. It is not just passive residency.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4e6b29b7-edf5-4ec2-9cb8-ea82fc44b7cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [I Criticize America Because I Chose It](https://substack.com/redirect/4e6b29b7-edf5-4ec2-9cb8-ea82fc44b7cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Jan 5
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4e6b29b7-edf5-4ec2-9cb8-ea82fc44b7cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Over the years, we have watched a dismantling of constitutional rights, slanted for political purpose, slowly eroding the fundamentals of what it means to be American and in the USA.
And the idea of being American is something we have to hold dear and reinforce fervently, so everybody can understand why we are here, what we are working for, and what we are working toward.
Like everything. If you do not use it, you lose it.
If you do not teach it, you forget it.
If you do not practice it, it is lost.
Our rights work the same way. Rights that are only theoretical are rights that are already halfway gone.
That is why I talk about them like muscles, because the moment the habit disappears, the erosion starts.
### The First Amendment Got Turned Into a Subscription Service
The First Amendment has been debated differently ever since we gained the ability to broadcast to the masses. There have always been debates about what is acceptable in public and what is not.
Freedom of speech has always been contested.
What does it mean? Is it only about government? Is it about escaping consequences? Is it about what can be on television? What can be on radio? What counts as "adult," what counts as "appropriate," and can be broadcast over the airwaves?
And then there is speaking out against your government. Questioning so-called conventional wisdom. That has also been under debate.
But the internet changed the structure of the debate.
Because speech moved from the halls of Congress, the public squares, and the laws of the Supreme Court into the terms and services of corporations. Into privately held walled gardens. Into communication lines that run on subscriptions and monetized distribution.
Pay to play.
Pay to speak.
Speech costs money now. And the more money you have, the more speech you get. [Citizens United](https://substack.com/redirect/41bc5f66-a913-42a1-a930-1fbd3f11fdb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sits right inside this reality. You buy ads and push them through the same rails and walled gardens.
The incentives to speak up or stay quiet are monetized. Certain words get discouraged. Certain words get beeped. People self-censor. And we now debate consequences of speech **more than the freedom we are supposed to be protecting.**
People repeat the phrase "freedom of speech does not mean freedom of consequences," and sometimes it is true. But consequences are now used as a tool to get around the freedom itself.
That is not principle. That is control.
### The Fourth and Fifth Amendments Got Quietly Rewritten by Data
The Fourth and Fifth Amendments have always been fascinating to me because they are supposed to protect against overreach.
Search and seizure.
Due process.
The right to plead the Fifth and not incriminate yourself.
But have they been bent too? I do not think everybody noticed.
Data is a new form of self-incrimination that people did not anticipate.
Search and seizure used to be your house and your car. Now it is opening your phone. Now it is looking through your data. Mining your emails. Training AI with content you created.
And it is all treated as acceptable because terms and services exist, and people clicked "agree."
Sure, we can nitpick the letter of the law and say the state still needs a warrant to enter your home. [Which for some reason that is up for debate.](https://substack.com/redirect/8333d732-82e9-4c4b-9e81-e07cb507e510?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) But the real fight is what "unreasonable" means now, and what power can justify as normal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e8c8147f-a615-434b-ad28-0646f6eb965b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[NPR Artice](https://substack.com/redirect/8333d732-82e9-4c4b-9e81-e07cb507e510?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Patriot Act after 9/11 opened the door to expanded definitions. What is reasonable? What is terrorism? Who counts as a terrorist? How flexible is that label when someone wants to make you feel safe?
Safety becomes the justification for bending the rules.
And this is why that old line matters: Those who would give up essential liberty, to purchase a little temporary safety, deserve neither liberty nor safety.
The constitution did not protect you so that your data could become an evidence locker. So that your phone could be opened. So that you could be monitored, tricked into saying things without representation, incriminated by something you wrote 10 years ago in a text message drunk at 2am and used against you even if you did not understand the contract you supposedly entered.
### Surveillance Gets Sold as "If You Are Innocent, Shut Up"
Surveillance becomes "reasonable" the moment you frame it as catching bad people.
Cameras trained on AI on every city block and corner to monitor who comes in and out, sold under the guise of safety.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a8752fb-2a77-47e4-a6e6-602b75177876?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Flock Camera](https://substack.com/redirect/a92b8aae-0cf8-4eb1-95b7-8ca94e1eeb1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And then the line comes out.
If you are not a criminal, you have nothing to worry about. Just shut up and comply.
That is not the language of liberty. That is the language of a population being conditioned to accept monitoring as normal.
#### The Second Amendment Is the Moral Question America Cannot Avoid
Then we come to the Second Amendment which is one of the hardest to reconcile inside a country that deals with gun violence. But it sits deep within American culture, identity, and values.
To defend yourself.
To protect your family.
To protect your property.
And to protect against tyranny of government.
But in the wake of a country plagued with gun violence, that moral question that has sat with the United States since inception. One we wrestle with as a culture, as people, as communities, as families, as faith.
And it is easily spun for political purposes. Neither side is innocent.
The left asks, why do you need a gun? Why do you need to carry? People see a sidearm in a grocery store and panic. They judge. They label the person paranoid, stupid, or inciting violence.
But I go back to the earlier point.
If you do not practice and participate in your freedoms, you forget what they are, and they get taken quietly.
So I ask it directly.
Does the right to bear arms only apply when you feel safe and in a safe space?
Does it only apply when you are home alone?
Does it apply in a park?
In a grocery store?
**At a protest?**
Because if the Second Amendment was the fundamental amendment meant to keep a civilian populace armed against tyrannical government, then the entire point was that it matters most when things are unstable, not when things are comfortable.
And this year, 250 years after the founding of the United States of America, we keep referencing the question... When is the right time to have the firearm?
Was the right time to bear arms in a classroom to protect students from mass shooters, since the shooter has the right to bear arms in public?
Is the right time to debate mental illness and mental health and whether red flag laws are reasonable or an overreach?
Is the right time an armed civilian population coexisting with armed state-employed police and federal agents?
And if none of those are the right time, then I ask again. Why was the law created? Why was it written into the Bill of Rights?
If it only exists in theory, it is already being rewritten.
### The Core Problem: Rights Are Being Treated Like Political Tools
This is what I think has happened.
The United States has gotten lost in interpretation of the fundamental beliefs we hold dear. Those beliefs are being treated more like political tools and debate topics for lawyers than the foundation of a culture, a civilization, a government, and the will of the people.
The gray areas and lines get crossed over and over again, pushing interpretation left and right to justify the erosion of said rights.
And when Congress cannot strip those rights away directly, because we **do** have a Constitution, corporations and terms of service and walled gardens pick up the slack.
That is the modern bypass.
### The Constitutional Crisis Is Bigger Than One Date
The constitutional crisis does not start with say January 6, or 9/11 and end whenever someone wants to say it ended.
It did not end when social media proved it can manipulate speech through algorithms.
It did not end when it became obvious your data is being weaponized against you, not by accident, but by design.
And it does not end when Second Amendment rights are now in question, even though that is literally the scenario they were created for.
This is long-term erosion, dressed up as convenience, safety, and modernity.
### Do Not Build Your Worldview From a Single Incident
I urge people not to form sweeping opinions off individual cases, individual incidents, and videos on the internet.
Dig deeper.
Analyze the fundamental building blocks of the nation, the culture, the government, and power as the people.
Then look at whether everything we are doing now, everything we have done up to this point, and the way everything is headed supports our core tenants and core beliefs.
If we are going to keep these rights, they have to be taught. In schools and at home.
Not just reading the words. Understanding what the words mean.
Understanding that freedom of speech is still freedom of speech when you are protesting in front of officers and federal agents.
Understanding that the right to bear arms is not a right you get only when the state feels comfortable.
Understanding that you cannot be searched unreasonably for walking down the street.
These things have to be internalized, not memorized.
### Freedom Makes Everything Harder, and That Is Why It Matters
Here is the part people do not want to admit.
**The laws of freedom make things harder.**
They complicate law enforcement.
They complicate policing the internet.
They complicate messaging.
They complicate **everything**.
Freedom is not efficient. It is not cheap. It is not safe. It takes more time. It takes more education. It requires restraint and sophistication and tools that allow jobs to be done without infringing on rights.
That is harder. That is more expensive. That is slower.
And over and over, we are seeing it is worth it.
Because the easy way is always the same. You give up liberty for convenience. You accept surveillance for safety. You accept monetized speech because it is "private." You accept erosion because it is gradual.
And then one day, you realize what you gave up is not coming back.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/194d72f9-e1b1-4547-a68e-282b504916f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Andor and the Mechanics of Authoritarianism](https://substack.com/redirect/194d72f9-e1b1-4547-a68e-282b504916f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
We must fight for these rights **fundamentally**.
It does not matter who allows them to be lost: the left or the right. Because when they are gone, they are gone.
That means practicing them, teaching them, and understanding them as constraints on power, not as political tools to be picked up and put down.
It means returning to the founding principles of what governs us and how we want to be governed.
And it means thinking with complexity, because complex problems require complex thought, and politics simplifies on purpose.

The Constitution Is Not a Vibe | | | Jan 27 | | | | | | | | | | | | What are the fundamental principles we are governed by and expected to live by? | | ---|---|--- Because when you lose clarity on that, everything else collapses into confusion. Personal life. Home life. Civil engagement. Without a moral compass, you do not know where to go. That is why I keep coming back to the Bill of Rights. The founders wrote constraints into the Constitution to govern how we interact with each other and what kind of state we live in. When you boil it down through all the nonsense, all the points of view, all the slants and twists, the outline is fundamental, clear, and true. And right now, we are losing that clarity. Narratives Are Winning Because Truth Is Getting Rebuilt I am watching people obsess over individual incidents and treat them like the whole story. Zooming in on videos. Rewinding. Picking apart frames like it is courtroom evidence. At the same time, I am already seeing AI reconstruct those same videos in different ways, packaged for propaganda and political slants. If you let your beliefs be built from isolated clips, and those clips can be rebuilt by for an agenda to match whatever story someone wants to sell, you are not thinking anymore. You are being guided. The answer is not to pretend the slants do not exist. The answer is to anchor back to the founding principles of what governs us and how we want to be governed. We Are Losing Our Way I have been saying for a long time that we have been losing our way. Political slants and jockeying have made us more confused, not more informed. I believe the Bill of Rights is deep-seated in the consciousness of Americans, so much so that many people think it is universal truth. As if it is not specific to one nation. But it is. It is universal for us, but not for other nations. That is part of what gives this country strength. It creates a unique individual sense of identity and governing rules that are supposed to be unbendable. But they are being bent. And when those rules become flexible, the idea of what it means to be American becomes hazy. It becomes a costume instead of a civic identity and responsibility. Rights Are Not Always Convenient, and That Is the Point We have to get back to understanding that these rules will not always serve your political purpose in the moment. They will be uncomfortable. They will hurt some people and benefit others at certain times. They are a building block that everyone has chosen to participate in. I emphasize chosen because I have said before why I criticize America. I criticize it because I choose to live here. That choice is conscious. It comes with obligations. It is not just passive residency. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Jan 5 | Over the years, we have watched a dismantling of constitutional rights, slanted for political purpose, slowly eroding the fundamentals of what it means to be American and in the USA. And the idea of being American is something we have to hold dear and reinforce fervently, so everybody can understand why we are here, what we are working for, and what we are working toward. Like everything. If you do not use it, you lose it. If you do not teach it, you forget it. If you do not practice it, it is lost. Our rights work the same way. Rights that are only theoretical are rights that are already halfway gone. That is why I talk about them like muscles, because the moment the habit disappears, the erosion starts. The First Amendment Got Turned Into a Subscription Service The First Amendment has been debated differently ever since we gained the ability to broadcast to the masses. There have always been debates about what is acceptable in public and what is not. Freedom of speech has always been contested. What does it mean? Is it only about government? Is it about escaping consequences? Is it about what can be on television? What can be on radio? What counts as "adult," what counts as "appropriate," and can be broadcast over the airwaves? And then there is speaking out against your government. Questioning so-called conventional wisdom. That has also been under debate. But the internet changed the structure of the debate. Because speech moved from the halls of Congress, the public squares, and the laws of the Supreme Court into the terms and services of corporations. Into privately held walled gardens. Into communication lines that run on subscriptions and monetized distribution. Pay to play. Pay to speak. Speech costs money now. And the more money you have, the more speech you get. sits right inside this reality. You buy ads and push them through the same rails and walled gardens. The incentives to speak up or stay quiet are monetized. Certain words get discouraged. Certain words get beeped. People self-censor. And we now debate consequences of speech more than the freedom we are supposed to be protecting. People repeat the phrase "freedom of speech does not mean freedom of consequences," and sometimes it is true. But consequences are now used as a tool to get around the freedom itself. That is not principle. That is control. The Fourth and Fifth Amendments Got Quietly Rewritten by Data The Fourth and Fifth Amendments have always been fascinating to me because they are supposed to protect against overreach. Search and seizure. Due process. The right to plead the Fifth and not incriminate yourself. But have they been bent too? I do not think everybody noticed. Data is a new form of self-incrimination that people did not anticipate. Search and seizure used to be your house and your car. Now it is opening your phone. Now it is looking through your data. Mining your emails. Training AI with content you created. And it is all treated as acceptable because terms and services exist, and people clicked "agree." Sure, we can nitpick the letter of the law and say the state still needs a warrant to enter your home. But the real fight is what "unreasonable" means now, and what power can justify as normal. | | ---|---|--- The Patriot Act after 9/11 opened the door to expanded definitions. What is reasonable? What is terrorism? Who counts as a terrorist? How flexible is that label when someone wants to make you feel safe? Safety becomes the justification for bending the rules. And this is why that old line matters: Those who would give up essential liberty, to purchase a little temporary safety, deserve neither liberty nor safety. The constitution did not protect you so that your data could become an evidence locker. So that your phone could be opened. So that you could be monitored, tricked into saying things without representation, incriminated by something you wrote 10 years ago in a text message drunk at 2am and used against you even if you did not understand the contract you supposedly entered. Surveillance Gets Sold as "If You Are Innocent, Shut Up" Surveillance becomes "reasonable" the moment you frame it as catching bad people. Cameras trained on AI on every city block and corner to monitor who comes in and out, sold under the guise of safety. | | ---|---|--- And then the line comes out. If you are not a criminal, you have nothing to worry about. Just shut up and comply. That is not the language of liberty. That is the language of a population being conditioned to accept monitoring as normal. The Second Amendment Is the Moral Question America Cannot Avoid Then we come to the Second Amendment which is one of the hardest to reconcile inside a country that deals with gun violence. But it sits deep within American culture, identity, and values. To defend yourself. To protect your family. To protect your property. And to protect against tyranny of government. But in the wake of a country plagued with gun violence, that moral question that has sat with the United States since inception. One we wrestle with as a culture, as people, as communities, as families, as faith. And it is easily spun for political purposes. Neither side is innocent. The left asks, why do you need a gun? Why do you need to carry? People see a sidearm in a grocery store and panic. They judge. They label the person paranoid, stupid, or inciting violence. But I go back to the earlier point. If you do not practice and participate in your freedoms, you forget what they are, and they get taken quietly. So I ask it directly. Does the right to bear arms only apply when you feel safe and in a safe space? Does it only apply when you are home alone? Does it apply in a park? In a grocery store? At a protest? Because if the Second Amendment was the fundamental amendment meant to keep a civilian populace armed against tyrannical government, then the entire point was that it matters most when things are unstable, not when things are comfortable. And this year, 250 years after the founding of the United States of America, we keep referencing the question... When is the right time to have the firearm? Was the right time to bear arms in a classroom to protect students from mass shooters, since the shooter has the right to bear arms in public? Is the right time to debate mental illness and mental health and whether red flag laws are reasonable or an overreach? Is the right time an armed civilian population coexisting with armed state-employed police and federal agents? And if none of those are the right time, then I ask again. Why was the law created? Why was it written into the Bill of Rights? If it only exists in theory, it is already being rewritten. The Core Problem: Rights Are Being Treated Like Political Tools This is what I think has happened. The United States has gotten lost in interpretation of the fundamental beliefs we hold dear. Those beliefs are being treated more like political tools and debate topics for lawyers than the foundation of a culture, a civilization, a government, and the will of the people. The gray areas and lines get crossed over and over again, pushing interpretation left and right to justify the erosion of said rights. And when Congress cannot strip those rights away directly, because we do have a Constitution, corporations and terms of service and walled gardens pick up the slack. That is the modern bypass. The Constitutional Crisis Is Bigger Than One Date The constitutional crisis does not start with say January 6, or 9/11 and end whenever someone wants to say it ended. It did not end when social media proved it can manipulate speech through algorithms. It did not end when it became obvious your data is being weaponized against you, not by accident, but by design. And it does not end when Second Amendment rights are now in question, even though that is literally the scenario they were created for. This is long-term erosion, dressed up as convenience, safety, and modernity. Do Not Build Your Worldview From a Single Incident I urge people not to form sweeping opinions off individual cases, individual incidents, and videos on the internet. Dig deeper. Analyze the fundamental building blocks of the nation, the culture, the government, and power as the people. Then look at whether everything we are doing now, everything we have done up to this point, and the way everything is headed supports our core tenants and core beliefs. If we are going to keep these rights, they have to be taught. In schools and at home. Not just reading the words. Understanding what the words mean. Understanding that freedom of speech is still freedom of speech when you are protesting in front of officers and federal agents. Understanding that the right to bear arms is not a right you get only when the state feels comfortable. Understanding that you cannot be searched unreasonably for walking down the street. These things have to be internalized, not memorized. Freedom Makes Everything Harder, and That Is Why It Matters Here is the part people do not want to admit. The laws of freedom make things harder. They complicate law enforcement. They complicate policing the internet. They complicate messaging. They complicate everything. Freedom is not efficient. It is not cheap. It is not safe. It takes more time. It takes more education. It requires restraint and sophistication and tools that allow jobs to be done without infringing on rights. That is harder. That is more expensive. That is slower. And over and over, we are seeing it is worth it. Because the easy way is always the same. You give up liberty for convenience. You accept surveillance for safety. You accept monetized speech because it is "private." You accept erosion because it is gradual. And then one day, you realize what you gave up is not coming back. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Jan 16 | We must fight for these rights fundamentally. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

name: Mark Kelly
subject: I’m suing Pete Hegseth
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth want to use the power of the White House and the Department of Defense to silence me because they don’t like what I have to say.
Team, it's Mark.
I am suing the Secretary of Defense.
After 25 years in uniform and another 5 in the United States Senate, I never imagined I’d have to do something like this. Hegseth has left me no choice.
Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth want to use the power of the White House and the Department of Defense to punish me because they don’t like what I have to say. Their attacks are directed at me right now, but they’re trying to send a message to every retired member of the military:
Speak out against us and we will come after you with every tool we have at our disposal. We’ll censure you, we’ll threaten your rank and retirement, and we might even court-martial you.
It’s unconstitutional, so I’m suing them. Beyond this lawsuit, it’s important we send a message to Trump and Hegseth to show them just how many people are on this team to defend constitutional rights. That’s where you come in.
I’ve been truly humbled by the support people have sent my way over the past couple of months. It means the world to me that so many of you care about what Trump and Hegseth are trying to do.
That’s how we’ve made it this far, and it’s how we’ll get to the other side of this chapter in our nation’s history. Together.
If you’ve been waiting for the right time to make a stand and join the fight, this is it.

| | Hi Peter,
Last week, With Honor Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott spoke with Lt. Col. Kyrylo Berkal, a Deputy Commander of Ukraine’s Third Army Corps, fresh from the front lines of the war.
For more than a decade, LTC Berkal has served Ukraine, including enduring brutal imprisonment after Russian forces captured Mariupol. Today, he leads Ukrainian forces across more than 200 kilometers of active front lines. Outnumbered and outgunned, his unit continues to hold the line through constant resolve and adaptability.
His message was simple and powerful: **f reedom endures when democracies stand together**.
You can watch his full comment [here](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=c8db5e5782&e=33f53a5b1a) or by clicking on the image above.
Thank you for standing with us,The With Honor Action Team
---
|
---
[|
---](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=9cede8ba02&e=33f53a5b1a)
| | With Honor Action stands with a broad coalition of veterans organizations in supporting a new bipartisan effort led by For Country Caucus member [Rep. Jack Bergman](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=1f23c55084&e=33f53a5b1a), Rep. Sarah Elfreth, and With Honor Action ally [Sen. Dave McCormick](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=206017f0c8&e=33f53a5b1a), and Sen. Jacky Rosen, aimed at expanding treatment options for veterans living with traumatic brain injuries.
As our Co-Founder and CEO, Rye Barcott, explains, the legislation**“aligns government, academia, and the private sector to accelerate research and treatment for traumatic brain injuries and reduce the skyrocketing suicide rates among active-duty service members and veterans**.”
His words capture why this effort matters: it brings together the strength of public and private innovation to deliver meaningful recovery and support for those who’ve served—especially where traditional approaches have too often fallen short.
📝 [Read the full article](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=36f0c25172&e=33f53a5b1a).
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=8f6d2d642f&e=33f53a5b1a)
| | “...the Chinese government has made its position clear: Critical minerals are not commodities to be traded but leverage to be used against the United States and our allies at the negotiating table. Until we solve this dependency, **the Chinese will weaponize it against us**.”
That’s what For Country Caucus member [Rep. Zach Nunn](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=c411229c13&e=33f53a5b1a), a currently serving Air National Guardsman, writes for the National Review. But the issue isn’t new to the For Country Caucus or to us.
Countering Chinese economic and trade strangleholds is a consistent priority for members of the For Country Caucus and our Senate allies, who have been working on legislation since [at least 2021](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=66082181d1&e=33f53a5b1a) to protect U.S. [pharmaceutical](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=527507a37f&e=33f53a5b1a) and [semiconductor](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=9cd5e2ed7f&e=33f53a5b1a) supply chains from Chinese influence.
Most recently, With Honor Action ally [Sen. Todd Young](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=6d791af0ca&e=33f53a5b1a) and Sen. Jeanne Shaheen introduced the [SECURE Minerals Act](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=bab236ac95&e=33f53a5b1a), which would strengthen America’s access to critical minerals by creating a Strategic Resilience Reserve to help stabilize markets, support domestic and allied production, and reduce reliance on China.
📝 Read more about the [SECURE Minerals Act](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=3fb32bdb43&e=33f53a5b1a).
