name: Mallory McMorrow
subject: Today, we’re talking cost of living
body:
[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?t=1001&akid=3895%2E898137%2EP6vL0E ][IMG]

Team,

You don’t need me to tell you that everything from groceries to gas to
childcare is too expensive. The rising cost of living is impacting all of
us in very real ways every single day.

I’m not interested in just talking about the problem. I’m reaching out to
tell you exactly what I plan to do about it.

I’m focused on an affordability agenda to help people get ahead, not just
get by.

I’m fighting to lower housing costs so you can have not just a house, but
the home you always wanted, expand access to childcare so you don’t have
to choose between kids and career, and make health care, prescription
drugs, and education more affordable so you can spend more time thinking
about the future than whether you can make ends meet. I know we can get it
done, and we're living proof right here in Michigan.

In the State Senate, we’ve passed legislation to raise the minimum wage to
$15 an hour and peg it to inflation moving forward so your spending power
keeps up with rising costs, protect our veterans and their benefits from
scammers, repealed the seniors’ pension tax and so much more.

This work doesn’t always make headlines, but you know what it does do? It
tangibly improves the quality of life for Michiganders. That’s what I’ve
accomplished in the State Senate. Now, I’m ready to bring the same
Michigan work ethic and aggressive affordability agenda to Washington —
because you deserve nothing less from your U.S. Senator.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-20260122-Endorse_copy/?refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260127_AM1_V1_S1&t=1002&akid=3895%2E898137%2EP6vL0E ]If you support my fight for affordability, will you personally endorse
my campaign for U.S. Senate today?

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-20260122-Endorse_copy/?refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260127_AM1_V1_S1&t=1003&akid=3895%2E898137%2EP6vL0E ]ENDORSE OUR CAMPAIGN

If you’ve been impacted by the affordability crisis, [ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-20260122-Endorse_copy/?refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260127_AM1_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=3895%2E898137%2EP6vL0E ]can you share your
story with me? It’s important to me that I don’t just have your support,
but you know you have mine too.

Thank you,

Mallory

subject: Steve Toth Campaign Meetup & Block Walk – This Saturday Woodlands and Kingwood
body:
Hello,
Thank you for your support of Steve Toth’s campaign. We truly appreciate your willingness to get involved.
I wanted to let you know that we will be holding a **campaign meetup and block walk in The Woodlands and Kingwood this Saturday at 10:00 AM**.
* **The Woodlands / Central Meetup**
We will be meeting at **Grace International Church** to kick off our block walk. This will serve as our main meetup location, where we’ll provide instructions, materials, and answer any questions before heading out.

**Information**
**Grace International Church**
**Address:** 24400 Interstate Hwy 45, The Woodlands, TX 77386
**Time: **Saturday Jan. 31st 10 AM
We will be meeting in the **Student Center**. Please park in the **front of the building** and follow the posted signs to the meeting location inside.
* **Kingwood Area**
For those who are located in or closer to **Kingwood** , we will also be hosting a **Kingwood-area block walk**. If you’re interested in participating in the Kingwood walk, please **email or text me directly** , and I will share the details with you.

**Information
Address:**** ** TBD ( Contact me for more information)
**Time:**** ** Saturday Jan. 31st 10 AM

**Contact Information:**
Phone: (512) 660-9565
Email: [Ben@stevetothforcongress.com](mailto:Ben@stevetothforcongress.com "mailto:Ben@stevetothforcongress.com")
There is **no expectation to stay the entire time** —you are welcome to join for as long as your schedule allows. We’ll make it easy for anyone who wants to help, whether it’s your first time block walking or you’ve done it before.
If you’re able to attend or would like more information, please feel free to reply to this email or call or text me directly.
Thank you again for your support, and I hope to see you on Saturday.

Best Regards,

Ben Cooper
Canvassing Director
Phone: (512) 660-9565 | Email: [ben@stevetothforcongress.com](mailto:ben@stevetothforcongress.com)

You could feel the prevailing public sentiment turn in real time.
Outrage over the killing of Alex Pretti reached athletes and influencers that ordinarily might try to steer away from politics. Dissections of the video were everywhere on cable news. The NRA said "Responsible public voices should be awaiting a full investigation, not making generalizations and demonizing law-abiding citizens."
You know it's bad when you've lost the NRA.
ICE killed the wrong human being. Alex Pretti has proven very difficult to caricature or villainize. Millions of Americans saw the video and concluded that he was an upstanding person trying to help another before being unjustly executed.
All of the more principled Republicans started making statements. Bill Cassidy claimed, "The credibility of ICE and DHS are at stake." David McCormick stated, "We need a full investigation into the tragedy in Minneapolis. We need all the facts." John Curtis wrote, "I disagree with Secretary Noem's premature DHS response, which came before all the facts were known and weakened confidence." Lisa Murkowski said, "The tragedy and chaos the country is witnessing in Minneapolis is shocking . . . a comprehensive, independent investigation of the shooting must be conducted . . . " This is the crew you look to to see if Trump is losing with moderate Republicans.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e4c0d38-da68-4cf9-b2fc-e2d5514c5bac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Trump has gotten the message. The first official to be scapegoated was Greg Bovino; the Border Patrol chief lost his commander-at-large role and left Minneapolis. Democrats have their sights set on DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, who doesn't have a lot of friends in Washington. What happens to the actual agent who shot Alex Pretti will take some time.
Trump called Tim Walz and Jacob Frey and posted a more conciliatory message on Truth Social. He dispatched Border Czar Tom Homan to run the operation in Minneapolis, presumably to tone down the approach.
He's going to need to do a lot more than that to calm the anger. Democrats are looking at the end-of-January shutdown as a real opportunity now to extract demands from Republicans who are quickly sinking in the public's estimation of how they are handling immigration, an issue they had a massive advantage on. There's also talk of impeaching Kristi Noem.
In my mind, the major flashpoint upcoming is whether Noem keeps her job. Trump will be loathe to show that much weakness by axing his DHS Secretary who has been a dogged messenger. On the other hand, Noem has rubbed various people in the administration the wrong way and is the most visible scapegoat given her reflexive defenses of ICE actions. Of Pretti, she said that he "committed an act of domestic terrorism" and "approached" agents while "brandishing" a 9mm semi-automatic handgun and was carrying "dozens of rounds of ammunition [to] inflict maximum damage on individuals and to kill law enforcement."
Anyone who saw the video knows that all of this is nonsense. We all know who Alex Pretti was - a selfless nurse who died trying to help others. The administration is losing on this one because people will still believe their own eyes.
To turn down the temperature in our country, check out [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/62e1d964-b642-4116-8bb4-518de1d0e5fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is trying to reduce polarization. To reduce your screen time, which can contribute to polarization in our own lives, check out [Noble Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/c35d3967-f4f1-4e7e-a097-a5cd72f12a60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Character still matters in the world, and that's a wonderful thing.

_I know better than most how competitive our statewide elections here in North Carolina can be._

We’re in the midst of the hardest fight of my career, and I won’t be able to win without help and support from across the country.

I’m running to be Georgia’s first Democratic governor in 30 years -- and I want to share with you about the journey that brought me here.

After I share my story, I’m going to ask you to donate to my campaign. It’s a longer email than I usually send, but I hope you’ll read it because this is personal to me. **My political heart changed because becoming a Democrat has made it easier for me to love my neighbor.** As a Republican, this was a daily struggle.
* **More than ten percent of Georgians are uninsured** \-- and Republicans’ refusal to extend Affordable Care Act tax credits will drive that number even higher, forcing more of our neighbors to make impossible decisions when they get sick.

* **Nearly twenty percent of children in Georgia lack consistent access to food** \-- and Republicans have made the problem worse by slashing funding for SNAP and programs that provide meals to kids in school.

* **Georgians are facing an affordability crisis,** with prices skyrocketing for essentials like food and housing -- but Republicans lack the courage to stand up to Trump and his reckless tariffs.

For decades, Republicans have told people without health insurance, food security, or access to housing to just “get a job.” But I know first-hand what it’s like to struggle to support a family on a budget -- _even with both parents working._

**Now, as a proud Democrat, I wake up every day with a better set of tools to serve those in need and to fight for the people of Georgia.**

As Governor, I’ll set the priorities for our state, and I believe we should help our neighbors who need it the most. But first we need to win -- and I can’t do it with your help.

name: Ted Cruz
subject: Re: Elizabeth Warren
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
Democrats just raised an ADDITIONAL $7 MILLION to buy our Senate seat in Texas.

| | | [](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)
---
| | Fellow Conservative, I'll cut right to the chase... Democrats just raised an **ADDITIONAL $7 MILLION** to buy our Senate seat in Texas. And it gets worse: Elizabeth Warren personally wrote a massive check to the Texas Democratic Party (and many others). Here's what she said: **_" They need money NOW to hire staff, recruit volunteers, knock on doors, make calls, do all the things that make Democrats competitive in these elections."_** They're acting like the election is happening **tomorrow**. We should be moving along with the same sense of urgency. **__Because Fellow Conservative, we also need to hire staff, recruit volunteers, knock on doors, and make calls_. _** Meanwhile, too many of us are acting like we have all the time in the world. [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/70ea543a-8b32-4af7-be2a-5faf7c90b038?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Society of the Spectacle](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/63ef4f5c-c4e4-46e6-9e74-24919d999585?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , Guy Debord (1967)
> _**" We live in a [spectacular](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6f967502-2bdc-449b-a1bc-e48149f6f667?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) society, that is, our whole life is surrounded by an immense accumulation of spectacles. Things that were once directly lived are now lived by proxy. Once an experience is taken out of the real world it becomes a commodity. As a commodity the spectacular is developed to the detriment of the real. It becomes a substitute for experience...sometimes we are the commodity and sometimes the consumer." **-- Lawrence Law, [Images and Everyday Life](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c56be517-a12b-4c6d-85ca-8d553dadb32a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)1_
* * *
**1.**
I learned of the violent killing of Renee Good through a text message from a friend, followed up with a frenetic barrage of videos from different angles of a woman being shot in the face three times, then drifting off, in a moving car, and seemingly crashing into a light pole.
My friend, K, immediately expressed outrage and demanded (or so his words made me feel) a reaction or response. I made a mistake that is all too easy to make in a tense political atmosphere. I jumped immediately into the legal and governmental ramifications.
I said that I wasn't surprised; given the extreme rhetoric in both parties, this was bound to happen soon. And that while it was a homicide, I couldn't tell from the videos that it was _murder_ ; it could be, you know, _self defense_. Plus, qualified immunity, supremacy clause, prosecutorial discretion, blah blah blah, and, in addition, I stressed: blah.
I went straight into LAWYER mode or, perhaps worse, FORMER CONGRESSIONAL CANDIDATE mode, and forgot, along the way, to be a human being.
K was not impressed. It's a sign of good fortune to have friends who hold you accountable to the minimum competency test of not being a dick. I was failing it.
* * *
**2.**
It began to dawn on me that I was consumed by concepts, totally numb to reality: a federal officer had killed a woman. Renee Good was dead -- and here, I thought also of [Charlie](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/68c749e1-da0b-4813-92a8-beed4c0eaf92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- the entire country watched the life go out of her body on social media.2 I felt a bit nauseous, so I tried to look up a picture just to connect with something, anything, less digital. More human.
I found this:
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f4fc13dc-98f4-4d97-9456-12f7d51c1867?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Courtesy: Romanucci & Blandin_
It wasn't the glossy, almost angelic one used in most national news coverage. Somehow this picture felt more real, perhaps because more mundane. The porcelain mug has a black cat (or is it an owl?) with big eyes, peeking out from a wicker basket. And it is inscribed with her name: Renee. With an accent on the second 'e.' I was wondering about that. I suspected journalists were misspelling it. Yeah, I thought, that matters. Gotta get her name right. Renee.
Sigh.
I felt a bit more like myself.
* * *
**3.**
Then I thought about the officer, Jonathan Ross. He's an Iraq War veteran and two-decade veteran of federal law enforcement.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/740bcdca-67b2-49b7-b9b1-50dfd51ab576?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Officer Ross and his wife. (Courtesy: La Derecha Diaro)_
To test whether [partisan brain rot](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1cc1ea1b-1f75-49ae-926d-92bea0fa482d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has totally destroyed your rational faculties, try to practice empathy for someone of the other tribe, even if you consider them blameworthy. If you can't, consider seeking help.3
Here I related somewhat to both victim and officer, but my friend and all the coverage rightly put my focus on Renee. She was dead.
What about Officer Ross though? Whatever happened next, I began to realize, his life would never be the same. After the j[ury pool has been so thoroughly contaminated by media](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fd279595-7730-4c3d-921b-27441456014e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), he may never get a fair trial. And in this administration, the victim's family may not even see a real investigation.4 Let alone a charging decision.
* * *
**4.**
We have a presumption of innocence in this country. It is a _formal_ , legal right; indeed, a constitutional one.
But it is also, and more importantly, a _cultural_ touchstone.
In the United States of America we tend to believe that it is _wrong -- _plainly _unethical_ -- to convict someone even in the _informal_ court of public opinion, in our hearts, in our perception of their character (i.e., reputation) without evidence, an opportunity to be heard, or at least some gesture at fairness. What is _fair_? That's harder to define.
[](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ab256cc1-2ac2-45c3-83c6-93aade77462c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
> _**" We all know, intuitively, if you start talking about punishment before trial even begins, you're putting the idea of guilt in the forefront of everyone's mind. Yet presumption of innocence is the foundation of our whole justice system. Without that, we're no better than totalitarian states who imprison and execute people on the whim of an all powerful leader."**_5 _-Attorney Alan Shore (James Spader), Boston Legal_
Jonathan Ross may have committed murder, or he may not have; he may, or he may not, be shielded from criminal liability by virtue of being an officer of the federal government, acting in the line of duty; and his use of lethal force in that situation may, or may not, be objectively reasonable.6
I don't know.
And I _cannot_ know.
Because I am neither a forensic expert nor a member of a jury, with access to _all_ the admissible evidence, watching _all_ the videos, from each and every available angle, hearing eyewitness testimony from officers and citizens. Absent more, I cannot and will not say that Johnathan Ross in fact murdered Renee Good. I can't and won't say his use of force was reasonable, either.
By deciding not to decide, I invoke a value strongly implied by the 1st amendment.
I like to call it the 1.5th Amendment: _my constitutional right to not have an opinion._

name: Britney VanCitters
subject: Re: Protect clean air & water — fund natural resources agencies
body:
Hi Peter,
I want to make sure you saw Eliza's last email. During the upcoming session we'll be working to call for full funding of Oregon’s natural resources agencies, and we can't do it without you. Will you join us in support? [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
When: Thursday, February 5th from 12-2pm
Where: Oregon State Capitol, Salem
RSVP here [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
Wear BLACK!
I hope to see you there,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Britney_signature-removebg-preview.png]
Britney VanCitters (she/her)
OLCV Political & Organizing Director [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Txv-EIYKCk6bDzVIkhWfpg2?contactdata=YnhxKPfOEMibBBk6DUcto0oFr8FQJAis4s8JcHlzB3xsn5ApDBVSgXIg5Tes7+3BOcQVxkrMbEGrK327JfoJ57PND2bWhPIZ1E7yCiwbyVnHRmMGAhTjDZmQ5GCVuQgw]
https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6 [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
Dear Peter,
OLCV is partnering with environmental and climate justice partners to call for full funding of Oregon’s natural resources agencies, and we need your voice there to get it done.
When: Thursday, February 5th from 12-2pm
Where: Oregon State Capitol, Salem
RSVP here [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
Wear BLACK!
In order to finance taxpayer handouts to powerful corporations and wealthy investors (included in Trump’s "Big Beautiful Bill"), Oregon lawmakers are considering cuts. And yet again, our natural resources agencies like the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) and Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) are on the chopping block. These agencies ensure that Oregonians have clean air and water, healthy oceans, and protected lands, and they are vital to our public health and community well-being. Our transportation and climate programs like heat pumps and electric vehicle rebates, are also on the line. Join us for a rally in Salem on Thursday, February 5th from 12pm-2pm. [https://forms.gle/MWdhyX53rvKBHREb6]
The climate justice, transportation, and conservation communities are coming together with a broad coalition of progressive partners to rally in Salem and show lawmakers that Oregonians are counting on them to fund essential agencies and programs. We will rally in solidarity with labor, education, hunger, immigration, housing, choice advocates, and more. We need YOU to show up big for climate, transportation, conservation, wildlife, clean air and water, and make sure we stand out in the crowd.
More specific details will be shared closer to the event. Please feel free to invite other climate advocates and activists in your networks-- the more the merrier!
In solidarity,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Eliza.png]
Eliza Walton (she/they)
OLCV Coalition Director [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Txv-EIYKCk6bDzVIkhWfpg2?contactdata=YnhxKPfOEMibBBk6DUcto0oFr8FQJAis4s8JcHlzB3xsn5ApDBVSgXIg5Tes7+3BOcQVxkrMbEGrK327JfoJ57PND2bWhPIZ1E7yCiwbyVnHRmMGAhTjDZmQ5GCVuQgw]

Donald Trump's assault on Minneapolis will be a landmark event in American politics. Everywhere right now, there's evidence that Americans who aren't Democrats or even Democratic-leaning are choosing to believe their own eyes over the administration's obviously false explanation for Alex Pretti's execution. Even the regime's strongest defenders--from the [NRA](https://substack.com/redirect/752346a6-e764-49a2-b831-a0cec131c4ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [Fox News](https://substack.com/redirect/056ae5d3-9fba-49e3-b742-bf5bd0131d91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--seem to be uneasy or downright unwilling to play along with Trump's lies about the murder his goons committed in broad daylight on Saturday. A quick look around [r/Conservative](https://substack.com/redirect/bcdfb905-c78e-45bb-b64f-13bd97f01cf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--the Reddit community for conservatives--shows that this reaction is far from isolated. Across the country, people who are in many ways as far removed from a resistance demonstrator as it's possible to be are coming to the same conclusion as your average No Kings participant: that this regime is dragging the U.S. into authoritarianism.
Trump is politically vulnerable right now. But what happens next depends in part on the opposition. If Democrats want to turn this moment into a real inflection point--permanently cratering Trump's popularity and MAGA's power--they need to go all in on this fight. The people of Minneapolis and others all across our country have already been throwing down in incredibly inspiring ways. It's time for our opposition party to join them.
Subscribe to receive new posts!
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE4NTk4NDk2NywicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc2OTUzNTc2MywiZXhwIjoyMDg1MTExNzYzLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.ZYiVdQMbVPBpHc0qUQ8SLAbnFPRST3N3xpOOQek43WQ?)
What does that mean for Democrats? The bare minimum requires refusing to hand billions of dollars more to the government agency openly executing people in the streets. This is nonnegotiable. And thankfully, in the wake of Alex Pretti's murder, Senate Democrats seem to be coalescing around that position. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/fd4af1cb-b1c4-4757-b3d3-b392801e7a95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Democrats will not vote for the DHS funding bill without changes to "restrain, reform, and restrict ICE." And with the government funding deadline approaching on January 30, if Schumer can effectively whip and unify his caucus--as Hakeem Jeffries [couldn't or wouldn't](https://substack.com/redirect/5d5ba998-af3e-4727-99db-28ef5cc6637b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week--that will mean a government shutdown.
Then what? One path forward would be for Democrats to follow the same playbook they used for the last shutdown--do some run-of-the-mill messaging, wait a couple weeks until enough Senate Democrats decide to give in, and then pass the offensive legislation unchanged. But what if we closed our eyes and imagined, for a moment, how a maximally effective opposition party might respond to these events? When I try this exercise, here's what I see.
When the government shuts down, Congressional Democrats head, en masse, to Minneapolis. "Trump's regime has launched an all-out attack on an American city--an attack that will be repeated against more of our communities if it's not stopped there," they announce. "Democrats are committed to protecting Americans from these assaults on our rights and our persons, so we are getting on a plane and going where those assaults are strongest." Wherever possible, they ask local reporters from their states or districts to join them on their trip, to communicate about the reality on the ground. (Some Democratic content creation teams might be a good idea, too.) When they arrive, Democratic leaders join in the frontline organizing happening in Minneapolis. They don't just stay for a quick photo op and then bail. They do ridealongs with "[commuters](https://substack.com/redirect/b6d216e2-7f28-4c92-90b5-ec73e1452bcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"--the activists following Border Patrol vehicles around the city. They join the [legal observers](https://substack.com/redirect/c468d8cc-7557-4906-9504-4eea91eecb02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recording clashes between Minneapolis residents and the militia forces occupying their city. They put on gas masks when ICE fires tear gas at them; they stand with [parents protecting their schools](https://substack.com/redirect/4d3aa3d1-3b52-4cc1-af71-70a5dfd86b9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This work would do three things. First, it would drive endless, round-the-clock coverage--not just in national media, but in hundreds of regional outlets covering local Democratic leaders--of Trump's violent goons doing all the horrific, un-American, Constitution-trashing abuses that most voters can't stomach.
Second, it would likely lead to some sort of win--even if it's just a full end to Trump's siege of Minneapolis--as Trump's approval ratings sink lower and lower and the regime recognizes the political damage they are doing to themselves. Seeing that Trump can really be beaten would further strengthen the resistance movement, as people sense a momentum shift.
And third, it would give Democrats an opportunity to show the American people that they do, in fact, have some backbone after all. This is one of the Democratic Party's key liabilities right now--it [lacks credibility](https://substack.com/redirect/6c684f8c-a31b-463d-a6c7-1e2e31d181a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A recent poll found that [fewer than one in five](https://substack.com/redirect/e4507610-8f7a-4546-a541-afec6fa8f27e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Americans believe the Democratic Party is the party that can "get things done." People don't believe Democrats will do what they say they'll do; they don't trust them to follow through, to stand up to power, to commit to fights. It's hard to think of a better solution to this problem than an explosion of content featuring Democratic leaders acting with what--to most non-MAGA voters--will be seen as undeniable courage, in opposition to undeniable tyranny.
Normal people appreciate seeing leaders actually walk the walk. When you watch someone put their body on the line to oppose something awful--even if it's someone you might have disliked before--you can't help but respect their chutzpah and commitment.
That respect is exactly what the Democratic Party lacks. It's what it needs to turn a vulnerable moment for this unpopular administration into a complete rout. The whole country is watching--why not demonstrate to America that, as Republicans skulk about in fear of displeasing their dear leader, Democrats have the courage to stand for their convictions?
You could say this vision is a naive daydream. Based on recent history, the idea that Democrats would display this kind of leadership right now is hard to imagine. And yet, there's nothing technically unrealistic, or even that challenging, about this strategy. It just takes some initiative and some bravery. That shouldn't be too much to ask, or demand, from our only opposition party. So let's demand it.
The Trump administration is waging a campaign of terror against its own population. They are [attacking](https://substack.com/redirect/6283a60f-5e68-48cd-a541-62b596a7dca8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) children, [abusing elders](https://substack.com/redirect/90c06bf0-37e6-49c4-be35-11caacd53120?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and treating an entire city of Americans like enemy combatants. They're trampling on the First, Second, and Fourth Amendments to the Constitution (at the very least). And now they're literally murdering civilians in the street. It's all too horrifying to fully comprehend. But there is one source of light in the darkness. The regime has miscalculated. They seem to have assumed that the American people are as deprived of humanity as they are. But they're not. Americans are repulsed by what's happening in Minneapolis, and they are putting the blame where it belongs. This could be Donald Trump's Waterloo. Let's press the attack.

On International Holocaust Remembrance Day, moments of symbolism matter--whether we notice them or not.
It is striking that **Sid Rosenberg** marked ten years on **WABC 77** today on the same remembrance day. It is not a coincidence. For many in this country without a voice, Jewish listeners and with his appointment to the Holocaust Memorial Council along with others like Siggy Flicker. Sid's tireless effort since October 7th has been a voice of light in darkness. He has used his voice and platforms, like his syndicated radio show, to honor history honestly in an era of forgetfulness or intentional revisionist history.
Contrast that with recent rhetoric from Minnesota Governor **Tim Walz** which is especially troubling.
Governor Walz again compared immigration enforcement by I.C.E to the experience of **Anne Frank** --a comparison he has made before, despite holding a master's degree focused on Holocaust education. _**This was not an off-hand comment born of ignorance. It was a conscious analogy, and therefore a conscious distortion.**_
If the governor is searching for guidance on immigration, he should look to his own party's recent leadership. Former President **Barack Obama** spoke clearly: a nation has borders, laws matter, and enforcement is not inherently immoral. Under his administration, deportations reached historic levels--not because of cruelty, but because governance requires balancing compassion with law & order. That historical record deserves honest examination, not erasure.

Every illegal immigrant, regardless of sympathy for individual circumstances, made an intentional act to enter the United States unlawfully. That fact can be debated, reformed, or criticized--but it remains a choice.
**The Jews who went into hiding had no choice.**
**A Real Life Holocaust Tale - Personal Experience Matters**
My grandparents were not "evading authorities." They were fleeing extermination. My grandmother was sent to a concentration camp at the age of fourteen. My grandfather lost his first wife and children to murder. After the war, he began again--meeting my grandmother and later having my mother in a displaced persons camp in Germany. My grandparents and mother came here as legal immigrants. They were stateless, traumatized, and alive only because the Nazis failed to finish the job.
**They did nothing wrong other than be born Jewish.**
To equate modern immigration enforcement--however flawed or in need of reform--with the systematic hunting of Jews across Europe is not just inaccurate. **It cheapens genocide which is the modern rhetoric**. It reduces the Holocaust to a rhetorical device, invoked when politically useful and discarded when inconvenient.
This selective use of Jewish suffering--deploying Jews when it serves a narrative and ignoring them when it does not--is not allyship. It is exploitation.
**Time for a PR Ceasefire**
**What must** _**not**_**happen next is a reckless escalation.** Calls to shut down the government over this issue would be catastrophic. The last shutdown driven by the political left was a disaster, harming workers, families, national credibility, and public trust. This country cannot withstand another shutdown--not economically, not socially, and not morally. Weaponizing dysfunction is not protest; it is negligence.
**America needs to wake up.**
We can all agree that protests, immigration enforcement clashes, and political rhetoric have spiraled out of control. A civic "protest ceasefire" would benefit the nation. _**But restoration requires seriousness, restraint, and historical honesty --not inflammatory Holocaust analogies and not self-inflicted governmental paralysis.**_
It also requires past presidents from both political parties to hold the line on their immigration stances and remind the public, republican or democrat - that illegal immigration has been an issue for both.
**A wake-up for the Jews of America and the World**
Perhaps this moment should serve as a wake-up call, particularly for progressives, including progressive Jews who still think their party is the party of JFK. Well it is not!
One of the few remaining voices in the Democratic Party speaking with clarity and moral consistency on Jewish issues is **John Fetterman** , who has deliberately distanced himself from agendas that instrumentalize Jewish history while abandoning Jewish safety. One of the Best victories in the 2024 Election was the re-election of John Fetterman over Dr. Oz. A lone soldier challenging the Squad and Others who are "pro-Palestine"
Clearly it was never about ending oppression and genocide in Iran, Syria as those same squad members are silent.
**In a time of darkness, it matters that there are still champions of Holocaust remembrance (and modern day anti-semitism) --people insisting on accuracy, dignity, and restraint. That insistence is not backward-looking. It is the foundation for drastic and necessary change.**
When everything becomes "like the Holocaust," then the Holocaust becomes nothing at all.
We owe the dead more than metaphors.
We owe the living a functioning country built on democracy.
And we owe history the truth.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

**A Bold Vision for the Future****Announcing My Run for San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors!** Dear Peter,I am excited to announce that **I am running for San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors** , District 4. This decision comes from a deep commitment to my community and a desire to continue working toward the future we all deserve.Together, we can build a county that offers opportunity, safety, and growth for every single person who calls San Bernardino County home. As a lifelong Inland Empire kid, this is deeply personal to me to make the place I call home work for all of us.
****
**The Threat to Our Democracy is Happening Locally Too**
As demonstrated by the passing of Prop. 50, people across this country**** are tired of the attacks on democracy. It is going to take strong leaders to protect our rights at all levels, even locally, and current leadership has proven they are not up to the challenge.
I’m battle tested: I was the President of one of the most contentious school boards in the country, Chino Valley, where I fought for families. I will bring the same spirit to this race as I challenge an out-of-touch MAGA career politician who has abused his office and ignored voters. He wasted taxpayer dollars, and increased his pay, all while families struggle to afford groceries and housing. He even tried to secede the County from California!
**A Record of Leadership**
As a longtime advocate for my community, I’ve spent years working to make a difference. Whether as a business leader, a school board member, or the Chair of the Chamber of Commerce, I’ve always been dedicated to standing up for what’s right. With a career of standing up to bullies and bringing people together, I can work to deliver results for the region I have always called home.
As the two-time Chair of the Chino Valley Chamber of Commerce, I’ve gone all in on developing our regional economy, helping bring millions of dollars for workforce programs.
As a school board member and Board President of the Chino Valley School Board, in even the most difficult of circumstances, I’ve demonstrated the kind of leadership that gets things done. I know how to fight for our families, like adding thirty minutes to the learning day to remediate learning loss.
**A Vision for Good-Paying Jobs and Economic Growth**
We all want a prosperous future for our families, and a major part of that is having access to good-paying jobs. I will work tirelessly to bring high-quality, sustainable jobs to the region, so residents can build careers and stay close to their families. By investing in local businesses and pushing for responsible growth, we can ensure a strong economy that works for all of us.
**It’s Time for Real Change**
Now, more than ever, we need leadership that doesn’t back down in the face of challenges, and that knows how to get results. I’m ready to bring this vision to the Board of Supervisors, and together, we’ll work to make the largest county in the United States a place of opportunity for all.
Today I’m humbly asking: [**Will you personally endorse my campaign and put a stop to the disastrous MAGA agenda here in San Bernardino County?**](https://christinagagnier.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe810d8b1ba298ccabc8f3ce7&id=43281dc956&e=0a3217b588)

clean_body: I'm Running for County Supervisor | | | | | | | | | | | | | A Bold Vision for the FutureAnnouncing My Run for San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors! Dear Peter,I am excited to announce that I am running for San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors , District 4. This decision comes from a deep commitment to my community and a desire to continue working toward the future we all deserve.Together, we can build a county that offers opportunity, safety, and growth for every single person who calls San Bernardino County home. As a lifelong Inland Empire kid, this is deeply personal to me to make the place I call home work for all of us. ** The Threat to Our Democracy is Happening Locally Too As demonstrated by the passing of Prop. 50, people across this country are tired of the attacks on democracy. It is going to take strong leaders to protect our rights at all levels, even locally, and current leadership has proven they are not up to the challenge. I’m battle tested: I was the President of one of the most contentious school boards in the country, Chino Valley, where I fought for families. I will bring the same spirit to this race as I challenge an out-of-touch MAGA career politician who has abused his office and ignored voters. He wasted taxpayer dollars, and increased his pay, all while families struggle to afford groceries and housing. He even tried to secede the County from California! A Record of Leadership As a longtime advocate for my community, I’ve spent years working to make a difference. Whether as a business leader, a school board member, or the Chair of the Chamber of Commerce, I’ve always been dedicated to standing up for what’s right. With a career of standing up to bullies and bringing people together, I can work to deliver results for the region I have always called home. As the two-time Chair of the Chino Valley Chamber of Commerce, I’ve gone all in on developing our regional economy, helping bring millions of dollars for workforce programs. As a school board member and Board President of the Chino Valley School Board, in even the most difficult of circumstances, I’ve demonstrated the kind of leadership that gets things done. I know how to fight for our families, like adding thirty minutes to the learning day to remediate learning loss. A Vision for Good-Paying Jobs and Economic Growth We all want a prosperous future for our families, and a major part of that is having access to good-paying jobs. I will work tirelessly to bring high-quality, sustainable jobs to the region, so residents can build careers and stay close to their families. By investing in local businesses and pushing for responsible growth, we can ensure a strong economy that works for all of us. It’s Time for Real Change Now, more than ever, we need leadership that doesn’t back down in the face of challenges, and that knows how to get results. I’m ready to bring this vision to the Board of Supervisors, and together, we’ll work to make the largest county in the United States a place of opportunity for all. Today I’m humbly asking: | | | | | | | | | | | | | Thank you for your support. It means the world to have you stand beside me in this race. subject: Hope is Something We Build Together
body:
| | | | | [|

| | | | | | Hi ,
I hope you are doing well in the midst of a truly horrific week and turning point in our country.
A lot has been happening in the news, and it’s been hard to keep up with sharing what’s happening on our very busy campaign. If you’re not following us on social media, that’s the best place to get more day-to-day updates and responses –because nobody wants or needs more clutter in their inbox!
In the meantime, I wanted to share a video of an interview I recently did with [Robert Hubbell](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=e38cc5f827&e=395a33a3d2), an American writer and commentator on societal issues. If you aren’t already subscribed to [Robert’s Today’s Edition Newsletter on Substack](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=6e515543df&e=395a33a3d2), you should be!
Robert is a true patriot and democracy defender who provides insightful commentary on what’s happening in our country. Just like me – he is an eternal optimist. So if you need a dose of hope in your life, read what he has to say below and [watch our short interview here](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=bac0821df0&e=395a33a3d2).
Be well, stay warm, and most importantly – never give up!
~ Kristin

| | ———From Robert Hubbell’s newsletter on 01/27:

Last week, I interviewed Kristin Hook, who is running for Congress in Texas CD 21—which is Chip Roy’s old seat. For those of you unfamiliar with Chip Roy, he was the most extreme member of the extreme Tea Party caucus in the House. He is not running for reelection in CD 21 because he is running to become Attorney General of Texas.That development, along with the redistricting Texas undertaken at Trump’s behest, has made CD 21 in Texas more competitive. Kristin Hook courageously entered the 2024 election against Chip Roy because no Democrat stepped up to challenge Roy. It was a brave act, and she learned much that will help her in 2026.Kristin has an impressive résumé and, as you will see in the interview below, she is thoughtful and passionate. If you are interested in supporting an effort to flip a seat in the Texas congressional delegation, I invite you to spend 15 minutes with me as I interview Kristin Hook.I had intended to run this last Sunday. As Kristin and I ended taping of the interview last Thursday, I said “ _I’ll run this on Sunday barring any major developments between now and Sunday_.” Sadly, ICE killed Alex Pretti on Saturday morning, so I delayed publication of the interview until today.Even if you’re not particularly interested in supporting a congressional candidate in Texas, I think the interview is still worth watching. body:
Join Our Autism Support Group!

We invite you to join our Autism Support Group on Wednesday, February 4th at 5:00 PM PST / 8:00 PM EST for a meaningful evening of connection, education, and community. These support groups are designed to provide a safe, welcoming space for parents, caregivers, and individuals impacted by autism and other neurological conditions to share experiences, ask questions, and feel supported on their journey.

We are honored to welcome Dr. Brian Hooker as our guest speaker for this session. Dr. Hooker is a respected researcher and advocate in the autism community, and he will share valuable insights and answer questions from attendees.

Whether you are just beginning your journey or have been advocating for your loved one for many years, this group offers a safe place to learn, connect, and grow together. We look forward to seeing you there!
REGISTER HERE (https://autismhealth.com/support/?mc_cid=0cf597662b&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** The 2026 Autism Health Summit is Almost Here!
------------------------------------------------------------

The Autism Health Summit is our flagship educational event, bringing together leading voices in research, medicine, advocacy, and integrative health for three powerful days of learning, connection, and collaboration. This annual gathering is designed for parents, practitioners, researchers, and advocates who are seeking deeper insight into autism and neurological health from a whole-body, whole-family perspective.

We are honored to welcome an extraordinary lineup of speakers, including Aaron Siri, Del Bigtree, Dr. Toby Rogers, Dr. Sabine Hazan, Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, Ed Clay, and many more respected experts and thought leaders. Together, they will explore cutting-edge research, clinical insights, environmental factors, and practical strategies that families and professionals can use. For a full list of speakers, click HERE to see our agenda (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/track.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fahsconference.com%252Fagenda%252F%2Fb43o%2FXYvCAQ%2FAQ%2Ffb66b930-9caa-4773-b075-95fc5d58a8e8%2F1%2FeR-lkap3k2/b43o/_wDDAQ/AQ/54bbc5f5-e544-4fbd-bdef-05b7cbaacdec/2/IpUuENx2MV?mc_cid=0cf597662b&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e57a03a4-6daa-4479-a794-45c77b5b1f0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ronald Reagan's 1980 coalition was a fusion of Barry Goldwater's 1964 [libertarian-conservative insurgency](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3110e485-d506-4068-af72-3fceed2ba306?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the populist energy of disaffected blue-collar Democrats. Goldwater had railed against the Eastern Establishment, the "dime-store New Deal," and the "Rockefeller Republicans" who treated conservatism as a country-club hobby. Reagan inherited that anti-elitist DNA but broadened it: tax revolt in California, evangelical turnout in the Sun Belt, Roman Catholics, and a visceral "Make America Great Again" before the phrase existed. The glue was Nixonian distrust of Washington insiders, foreign entanglements, and crony capitalism.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.nbKHiYwvCI0t5pPi6pM3EQDiRt7p3zpwPZ7uZuzu5o0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=185987767)
George H.W. Bush represented the precise antithesis. A Yale Skull-and-Bones patrician, former CIA director, and Trilateral Commission member, Bush embodied the very "kinder, gentler" managerial class that Goldwater-Reagan voters despised. His 1988 campaign leaned on Reagan's coattails, but the cracks were immediate. The 1990 budget deal--explicitly breaking the "read my lips" pledge--crystallized the betrayal. Pat Buchanan's 1992 primary challenge polled 37 percent in New Hampshire on a platform of economic nationalism and anti-NAFTA fervor.
Ross Perot siphoned another 19 percent nationally. The Reagan coalition did not merely lose; it shattered because the populist base refused to stomach elite compromise.
Fast-forward to 2016. Donald Trump's ascent replicated the Goldwater-Reagan formula on steroids:
* Economic nationalism (tariffs, immigration enforcement, China hawkishness)
* Anti-elitism (drain the swamp, fake news, deep state)
* Cultural traditionalism without theocratic overtones (school choice, law and order, Second Amendment absolutism)

Crucially, MAGA is not monochromatic. It contains four overlapping but distinct constituencies:
* America First nationalists - trade protectionists, border hawks, non-interventionists abroad, anti-Israel and everywhere else foreign aid.
* Independents - Obama-Trump voters in the Rust Belt who want competency, not ideology.
* Libertarians - tech-savvy, crypto-friendly, anti-lockdown, anti-Fed.
* Freedom First conservatives - limited-government purists who tolerate Trump's personality for judicial appointments and deregulation.

These groups cohere under the banner of anti-elitism. They will forgive almost any stylistic excess so long as the candidate fights the regime. The moment that fight is perceived as theatrical rather than existential, the coalition frays.
Enter the post-2024 landscape. The institutional GOP reasserts control via donor class pressure. The new leadership cadre--think a Nikki Haley, Brian Kemp, or a rebranded Ted Cruz--pivots toward:
* Resumption of pre-2016 trade orthodoxy ([USMCA](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8541d378-bbd4-4f5b-b1d3-1f36b5a36b32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tweaks, not tariffs)
* Re-engagement in Ukraine and Middle East quagmires under "rules-based order" rhetoric
* Soft-pedaling on Big Tech censorship and FBI reform to preserve donor relationships

Rhetorical nods to "working families" while advancing corporate tax gimmicks. Farmers for example can see the land grab of Big Tech after decades of Big Agriculture encroachment.
This is H.W. Bush's "kinder, gentler" conservatism updated for the TikTok era. It is competent, globally literate, and utterly uninspiring to the base that stormed the barricades in 2016. The telltale sign will be the 2026 midterms: if the GOP holds the House by threading the needle on abortion (federalism platitudes) while quietly advancing amnesty-lite "immigration reform," the populist revolt begins.
They view trade and immigration as zero-sum survival issues. A W Bush-style "compassionate conservatism" that pairs tax cuts for multinationals with guest-worker expansions is indistinguishable from Jeb Bush's 2016 platform. The Club for Growth will fund ads touting "free markets"; the base will hear "sellout to Beijing." The 2028 primary will feature a Doug Burgum or Glenn Youngkin promising "smart tariffs," and the response will be a third-party nationalist ticket polling 15-20 percent.
The Obama-Trump voter is transactional, not tribal. They want bridges fixed, fentanyl stopped, and grocery prices down. If the GOP reverts to Mitt Romney/Paul Ryan austerity (entitlement "reform" floated in 2025 budget negotiations), these voters return to Democrats or sit home. The 2022 Pennsylvania Senate race--Oz vs. Fetterman--showed that celebrity without economic populism loses swing voters even in red counties.
The lockdown wing of the GOP--parents radicalized by school boards, crypto investors furious at tech bros overreach--views the national security state as the primary threat. A Haley-esque foreign policy that pairs Taiwan saber-rattling with domestic digital-ID pilots will be seen as trading one tyranny for another. The Libertarian Party, moribund since 2016, suddenly clears 5 percent nationally with a [Dave Smith-type](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/42311f81-a845-42ba-8af9-e1d08944605e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) candidate.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=185987767&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1OTg3NzY3LCJpYXQiOjE3Njk1Mzc4MDQsImV4cCI6MTc3MjEyOTgwNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.p549Tb4tR8WMounEo03AAvsbhgvC67UoTi6l4-wj9ao)
Goldwater's ghost still haunts the movement. These voters tolerated Trump's deficits because tax cuts and deregulation outweighed fiscal scolds. But a return to Bush-Rove "compassionate conservatism"--Medicare Part D on steroids, faith-based initiatives 2.0--will trigger the Club for Growth defectors and the Ted Cruz holdouts. The House Freedom Caucus splinters; some join a populist caucus, others retire.
The 1990s analogy is instructive but ultimately too sanguine. George W. Bush and Karl Rove managed to paper over the evangelical-libertarian divide with:
* A muscular foreign policy (satisfying hawks)
* Tax cuts (placating supply-siders), debt retirement, spending reduction.
* Social-issue red meat (partial-birth abortion ban, marriage amendment)

The evangelical bloc, roughly 25 percent of the GOP primary electorate, accepted limited-government compromises because cultural conservatism was ascending. The libertarian wing grumbled but had nowhere else to go; Pat Buchanan's Reform Party imploded, and the LP never broke 1 percent.
MAGA's four factions, by contrast, are larger, more ideologically heterogeneous, and empowered by digital infrastructure. Some back-of-the-envelope math:
* America First nationalists: ~35 percent of GOP primary voters (per 2024 exit polls on trade/immigration)
* Independents: ~15 percent of general election deciders (Obama-Trump counties)
* Libertarians: ~10 percent (Paul delegate counts + Mises Caucus growth)
* Freedom First: ~20 percent (Freedom Caucus + Club for Growth overlap)

That is 80 percent of the activist energy. Unlike the 1990s, there is no single unifying issue (9/11, abortion, gay marriage) to cauterize the wound. The internet has obliterated gatekeepers; a Joe Rogan endorsement or Substack manifesto can launch a third-party bid overnight.
2026 Midterms - GOP holds House by 2-3 seats, Senate by 1. Leadership celebrates "bipartisan infrastructure" while quietly advancing a DACA deal. Base turnout collapses in special elections.
2027 Budget Fight - Speaker negotiates a continuing resolution that funds Ukraine at $60 billion and includes a "border security" package with 100,000 new visas. X erupts; #RINO trends for 72 hours.
2028 Primaries - Establishment consolidates behind a Kemp-Youngkin ticket. A nationalist (Vance?), libertarian (Massie?), and independent (RFK Jr. running as Republican?) split the vote. Winner ekes out 35 percent plurality.
General Election - Third-party nationalist polls 12-18 percent, libertarian 4-6 percent. Democrat wins with 46 percent in a five-way race. GOP loses House, Senate, and six governorships.
The Reagan-Bush rupture healed only because the Cold War provided an external enemy and because the populist energy was pre-internet, pre-talk radio, pre-Substack. Today's populists have:
* Alternative media ecosystems (Rumble, X, Telegram), Candace Owens, Tucker Carlson, Alex Jones, Steve Bannon etc.
* Decentralized fundraising (WinRed knockoffs, crypto PACs, Qatar)
* A generational memory of betrayal (2013 Gang of Eight, 2020 lockdowns, 2021 infrastructure bill, Leader Mitch McConnell)

The H.W. Bush accommodation worked once because the base had no megaphone. It will not work again.
Institutionalize economic nationalism: Codify China tariffs into law with sunset clauses tied to trade deficits. An AI arms race, data center dominance, and travel to Mars.
De-weaponize the state: Pass a federal civil-service reform bill capping FBI domestic surveillance authority. Repeal Obamacare, Patriot Act, The [National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act of 1986](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b666d6fb-9dc4-4a65-a5e8-ce97c424d709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and judicial restraint.
Decentralize cultural fights: Return education and health policy to states via block grants; defund federal agencies that enforce ideological mandates.
Embrace monetary populism: Audit the Fed, audit Fort Knox, explore a digital-assets framework that protects privacy.
None of these requires Trump's personality, but all require rejecting the donor-class consensus. Failure to do so guarantees a fracture.
The Reagan-Goldwater coalition tolerated H.W. Bush for one election cycle before exploding. MAGA is larger, angrier, and more ideologically diverse. The establishment's instinct--rebrand, moderate, manage--will accelerate the breakup. No Charlie Kirk discipline. Unlike the 1990s, there is no exogenous shock to unify the factions, no monopoly on communication, and no forgiveness for perceived surrender. The result will not be a mere primary challenge but a five-alarm political realignment whose aftershocks make the Bush-Rove evangelical detente look quaint. The only question is whether the GOP elite recognizes the cliff before or after the plunge.

body:
I am running for the United States Senate in Florida.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2407%2E135344%2EsKvfdT)

[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-vindman.TAdKXK&refcode=em260112-ebs-peltola&refcode2=2407.135344.sKvfdT&t=2&akid=2407%2E135344%2EsKvfdT)
---
My name is Alex Vindman, and after a lot of discussion, I have made the decision to run for Florida’s United States Senate seat.
I hope you will give me a chance to explain — but if you already know the importance of winning in Florida, then I am asking you to split a Founding Donation between my campaign and Elissa Slotkin today.
**[https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/alex-vindman](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/alex-vindman?t=3&akid=2407%2E135344%2EsKvfdT)**
Running for the United States Senate in Florida was not an easy decision. I knew the challenges going into this.
Ever since I blew the whistle on Donald Trump’s phone call with Ukraine, the president has had a vendetta against me. He attacks me every chance he gets on social media, and his billionaire allies will spend wherever it takes to pummel us in attack ads.
But as a former combat veteran in the United States Army, we don’t back down from a tough fight. We run towards it.
Our country is in chaos. While thug militias attack citizens and tariffs push prices sky-high, my opponent can’t seem to put public service before her own self-interest.

Peter, If you’re finding it hard to keep up with the rapid pace of the redistricting crisis that has unfolded over the last year, you’re not alone. Donald Trump and his state-level allies have been doing everything in their power to manipulate maps and unfairly tilt the scales in their favor for the 2026 midterms. So let’s go state by state to talk about where the fight for fair maps stands across the country. And yes, we need to ask you to [**make a donation to help power NDRC’s work to defend democracy everywhere it’s under attack.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124147060/597699402/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_StateOfPlay_email_20260127-NDRC-Tier1-StateOfPlay_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260127-NDRC-Tier1-StateOfPlay_&utm_campaign=StateOfPlay&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjExOTZmMDdiLWFkZmItZjAxMS04ZDRjLTAwMjI0ODJkMjc5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UyGxAOMbzF4gEdWK3LZt_Rs5hoA7VpPhzFFmtziZXNg=) **Florida**
The Sunshine State’s congressional map is already one of the most gerrymandered in the nation. But Gov. Ron DeSantis wants an even bigger power grab. He recently called for a special legislative session in April to _further_ manipulate the state’s map, in an effort to deliver up to 4 more seats to Republicans and undermine the representation of communities of color. **Kansas**
After proposing a new map that would eliminate the district of Rep. Sharice Davids, the state’s only Democrat in Congress, Republican state legislators are in full retreat. They admit they don’t have the votes to pass a new map, but there’s every reason to believe the White House isn’t giving up. **South Carolina**
We’ve seen mounting support for a mid-decade redraw from Rep. Ralph Norman, a Republican candidate for South Carolina governor, as well as from members of the Freedom Caucus. Now pushback from voters has forced the state senate leader to acknowledge that redistricting is now “unlikely” to happen in the current session. That said, this one isn’t over as Republicans are eager to target the district of Rep. James Clyburn, the only Democrat in the state delegation. **Missouri**
After the Republican-controlled legislature passed an egregiously gerrymandered map that could hand their party an additional congressional seat, more than 300,000 outraged Missourians signed petitions to put the map up for a vote. Republican state officials are trying every scheme imaginable to stop this citizen-led effort: They tossed out one-third of petition signatures and even admitted to writing the ballot initiative with misleading language. Trump allies are throwing millions into a campaign to thwart the will of the people, but the fair maps movement is fighting back to ensure Missouri voters get the final say. **Maryland**
Just last week, Governor Wes Moore’s Redistricting Advisory Commission voted to recommend redrawing Maryland’s congressional map to counter Republican power grabs in states like Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina. In stark contrast to those mid-decade redraws, the commission’s process was thoroughly transparent, and prioritized input from voters. **Virginia**
This month, state legislators passed a proposed constitutional amendment that would allow lawmakers to temporarily redraw the state’s congressional map, in an effort to even the playing field that is currently skewed due to Republican map manipulations in other states. Now, a measure to allow lawmakers to draw a new congressional map, will go to the voters — likely in April. Once again, where Democrats are countering the Republican power grabs, they’re doing it temporarily and with the express approval of the people. Sadly, that’s not all. Several other states are watching to see if the Supreme Court guts key parts of the Voting Rights Act to give them cover to redraw their own maps to favor Republicans and weaken minority voting power before the midterms. The fair maps movement will need to be ready for every outcome. [**In this moment of crisis, fighting for fair maps is an around-the-clock job — and we can’t do it alone. Whatever you’re able to give will make a HUGE difference in these states, and beyond.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124147061/597699403/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_StateOfPlay_email_20260127-NDRC-Tier1-StateOfPlay_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260127-NDRC-Tier1-StateOfPlay_&utm_campaign=StateOfPlay&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjExOTZmMDdiLWFkZmItZjAxMS04ZDRjLTAwMjI0ODJkMjc5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UyGxAOMbzF4gEdWK3LZt_Rs5hoA7VpPhzFFmtziZXNg=) | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

Now pushback from voters has forced the state senate leader to acknowledge that redistricting is now “unlikely” to happen in the current session. That said, this one isn’t over as Republicans are eager to target the district of Rep. James Clyburn, the only Democrat in the state delegation. Missouri After the Republican-controlled legislature passed an egregiously gerrymandered map that could hand their party an additional congressional seat, more than 300,000 outraged Missourians signed petitions to put the map up for a vote. Republican state officials are trying every scheme imaginable to stop this citizen-led effort: They tossed out one-third of petition signatures and even admitted to writing the ballot initiative with misleading language. Trump allies are throwing millions into a campaign to thwart the will of the people, but the fair maps movement is fighting back to ensure Missouri voters get the final say. Maryland Just last week, Governor Wes Moore’s Redistricting Advisory Commission voted to recommend redrawing Maryland’s congressional map to counter Republican power grabs in states like Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina. In stark contrast to those mid-decade redraws, the commission’s process was thoroughly transparent, and prioritized input from voters. Virginia This month, state legislators passed a proposed constitutional amendment that would allow lawmakers to temporarily redraw the state’s congressional map, in an effort to even the playing field that is currently skewed due to Republican map manipulations in other states. Now, a measure to allow lawmakers to draw a new congressional map, will go to the voters — likely in April. Once again, where Democrats are countering the Republican power grabs, they’re doing it temporarily and with the express approval of the people. Sadly, that’s not all. Several other states are watching to see if the Supreme Court guts key parts of the Voting Rights Act to give them cover to redraw their own maps to favor Republicans and weaken minority voting power before the midterms. # Treasury axes Booz Allen contracts over Trump tax leak
The Trump administration's Treasury Department **[canceled all contracts with consulting giant Booz Allen Hamilton on Monday,](https://substack.com/redirect/56129989-c88f-47f3-911d-cad72db4c87d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** citing the firm's failure to safeguard sensitive taxpayer data after an employee leaked President Trump's tax records to media outlets.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56129989-c88f-47f3-911d-cad72db4c87d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Contracts terminated immediately:** Treasury ended 31 active deals with Booz Allen, worth $4.8 million annually and $21 million in total obligations, effective immediately.
* **Leak tied to ex-employee:** The action stems from contractor Charles Littlejohn, who previously disclosed confidential IRS records--including Trump's and those of billionaires like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos--to news organizations.
* **Security failures highlighted:** Treasury accused Booz Allen of inadequate safeguards for sensitive taxpayer information accessed via IRS contracts, eroding public trust in government data handling.
* **Stock impact severe:** Booz Allen Hamilton shares plunged over 8% following the announcement, amid broader Trump administration scrutiny of federal consulting contracts.

Earlier this month, six prosecutors quit the DOJ in protest over the Trump administration’s push to investigate the widow of ICE shooting victim Renée Good, instead of investigating the shooting itself.
Then, this Saturday, federal agents killed another American. Alex Pretti posed no threat and did nothing wrong.
On that same day, Attorney General Pam Bondi sent a ransom note to Minnesota’s governor demanding the state’s full, unredacted voter roll — Social Security numbers, driver’s license data, party affiliations — under the guise of “election integrity.”
Her price for “ending the chaos”? Handing over the personal data of every Minnesota voter.
I’ve seen this corruption firsthand. When the administration tries to spin the law to fit a political agenda, it betrays the public trust.
I joined the Marine Corps after 9/11 and later became a federal prosecutor. I swore oaths to defend this country and to uphold the law — not to serve a political party or a single man.
So when Donald Trump pressured my office to drop a case to protect an ally, I refused. Civil servants work for the people — not for one man and his destructive agenda.
Let me be clear: **My oath is to justice. I stand with every official who upholds it, against the intimidation that twists it, and with every community harmed when that oath is broken.**
We need more leaders who will put their oath before politics — leaders who will stand up and push back when the law is being twisted into a weapon.
**That’s exactly why I’m running for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 7th District.**

subject: ⏰ Tell Your Senators: No Raise for ICE!
body:
☎️ Peter, your Senators need to hear from you! | | | Peter, Over the weekend, as hundreds of thousands of our neighbors braced below-zero temperatures to demand an end to the terror ICE has unleashed in our communities, federal agents took yet another life. Alex Pretti was a son, a loving neighbor, and an ICU nurse who cared for our country’s veterans. **His death is a striking reminder of what we’ve known all along — ICE and CBP do not keep us safe.** This tragedy comes just weeks after the fatal shooting of Renee Nicole Good, the deaths of Keith Porter in Los Angeles and Silverio Villegas Gonzalez in Illinois, and over 30 deaths in 2025 and 6 deaths so far in 2026 of individuals at hands of ICE custody. **⏰ Despite these violent attacks, the House of Representatives voted last week to give ICE a raise, despite their already billion-dollar budget!** That’s billions of dollars that will never make its way down to our communities and the resources that truly keep us safe. Enough is enough!**** There is no place for violence in our cities and no excuse to fund an agency that kills mothers and fathers in cold blood and vanishes preschoolers from their communities.[ clean_body: ☎️ Peter, your Senators need to hear from you! | | | Peter, Over the weekend, as hundreds of thousands of our neighbors braced below-zero temperatures to demand an end to the terror ICE has unleashed in our communities, federal agents took yet another life. Alex Pretti was a son, a loving neighbor, and an ICU nurse who cared for our country’s veterans. His death is a striking reminder of what we’ve known all along — ICE and CBP do not keep us safe. This tragedy comes just weeks after the fatal shooting of Renee Nicole Good, the deaths of Keith Porter in Los Angeles and Silverio Villegas Gonzalez in Illinois, and over 30 deaths in 2025 and 6 deaths so far in 2026 of individuals at hands of ICE custody. ⏰ Despite these violent attacks, the House of Representatives voted last week to give ICE a raise, despite their already billion-dollar budget! That’s billions of dollars that will never make its way down to our communities and the resources that truly keep us safe. Enough is enough!** There is no place for violence in our cities and no excuse to fund an agency that kills mothers and fathers in cold blood and vanishes preschoolers from their communities. Thousands of working people across the country have written letters to their members of Congress to demand no more money for ICE. However, with the House of Representatives choosing to fund murder on our streets over the safety and dignity of our communities, we need everyone to make their voices heard. That’s where you come in, Peter. The Senate has the power to stop this wasteful, deadly use of our taxpayer dollars right now, before another life is taken. 👉 Will you make a call to your Senators today?** Dial 1-281-306-4198 , and find a script to help you make your call. In unity, Aria and the United We Dream team | Follow us on: | | | | |

subject: Trump is still lying about Michigan
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR
body:
Trump won’t stop pushing the Big Lie.
# [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/203?t=1&akid=1439%2E181023%2EV5tLry)
Friend,
Donald Trump is _still_ spreading the Big Lie that the 2020 election was rigged against him and that he won. He told the _New York Times_ earlier this month that he regrets not sending in the National Guard to seize voting machines in the states where he lost — including Michigan.
Trump made Jocelyn one of his prime targets in his election loss, falsely accusing her of election misconduct. When she oversaw the certification of Michigan's results, armed pro-Trump demonstrators showed up at her house, where she was home alone with her young son.
But Jocelyn stood firm against Trump, against his lawsuits, and against his threats to voting integrity.
With Trump back in the Oval Office, Jocelyn has continued to fight his efforts to interfere in our voter registration systems and rig elections in his favor. She fought against his demand for full voter registration data from Michigan, including sensitive personal information like the last four digits of Social Security numbers.
**With Jocelyn as governor, we know we have a leader who will stand up to this president, his administration, and anyone who tries to take our freedoms away from us.**
**[But she can’t win this race alone, so please pitch in right now to help her stand up to attacks on our democracy.](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q12026.Dfun4A&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260127_PM1_V1_S1&t=2&akid=1439%2E181023%2EV5tLry) **
