_On January 15, the Trump administration unveiled what it grandly labeled**" The Great Healthcare Plan,"** a proposal that promises lower costs, greater transparency, and more "consumer choice" in American healthcare. Strip away the branding, however, and the plan amounts to a familiar Trump-era formula: deregulation wrapped in slogans, thin on specifics, heavy on disruption. The proposal emphasizes insurer and hospital transparency, targets pharmacy benefit managers, and replaces traditional insurance subsidies with individual healthcare vouchers and expanded Health Savings Accounts. What it notably fails to do is explain--at a policy, clinical, or operational level--how seriously ill patients are supposed to navigate this system, how risk pools remain stable, or how physicians already drowning in administrative work are expected to absorb yet another layer of complexity. As with so many Trump initiatives, the plan gestures toward reform while outsourcing the consequences to patients and frontline providers. What follows is a physician's view from inside that reality._
##### **Dr.[Eric Lullove](https://open.substack.com/users/66521654-eric-lullove?utm_source=mentions), wrote this article and Blue Amp Media is publishing it here with permission.**
##### _**by Dr. Eric Lullove**_
For those of us in the trenches of private practice--navigating the labyrinth of Medicare LCDs, fighting the "death by a thousand cuts" of prior authorizations, and watching administrative bloat swallow clinical outcomes--the latest healthcare proposal from the Trump administration feels like a case of _d eja vu_.
They're calling it **" The Great Healthcare Plan."** But as a physician who spends as much time reviewing reimbursement policy as I do treating complex wounds and complex patients, I have to ask: Where is the actual _healthcare_ in this plan?
What we've been presented with isn't a blueprint for clinical excellence or system-wide stability. It's a deregulatory framework disguised as "consumer choice," and it risks leaving both patients and providers in a precarious position.
* * *
**The Anatomy of the Proposal**
The administration's January 15 rollout centers on four primary pillars. On the surface, some of these sound like the common-sense reforms we've been advocating for in the wound care and medical communities:
* **Transparency over Profiteering:** The "Plain English" standard for insurers and hospitals is a move toward exposing the opaque "spread pricing" that keeps patients in the dark.
* **Targeting the Middlemen:** There is a renewed focus on Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) and broker kickbacks--the administrative parasites that inflate costs without adding a single gram of clinical value.
* **The Voucher Pivot:** This is the most radical shift. The plan effectively ends direct subsidies to insurance companies, instead funneling that capital directly into Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) or "Healthcare Vouchers" for individuals.

* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.IE_QCzcKjTQ2PcmlLjutGB4CQQDIAWn3Fb1955MZz04?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186014565)
* * *
**The Pros: Shining a Light on the "Black Box"**
There are elements here that make sense. **Price transparency** is long overdue. If we are forced to justify every CPT code and CTP application with mountain-high documentation, it is only fair that hospitals and insurers are forced to show their hand regarding profit margins and denial rates.
Furthermore, the $50 billion commitment to **Rural Healthcare** --leveraging the _Working Families Tax Cuts Act_ --is a necessary acknowledgement that our rural infrastructure is on life support. Investing in tech and facility modernization is a win for access, provided the money actually reaches the bedside.
* * *
**The Cons: The Administrative Burden and the "Death Spiral"**
Here is where the clinical reality clashes with the political "concept." As someone who understands the intricacies of the CMS fee schedule, I see several red flags:
* **The "Consumer" Fallacy:** The plan treats healthcare like a retail commodity. Expecting a patient with a chronic limb-threatening ischemia or a complex wound or even having a heart attack or stroke to "shop around" with a voucher is not just unrealistic; it's dangerous. Healthcare isn't a luxury watch or a high-end espresso machine; it is a necessity that often requires immediate, expert intervention.
* **Fragmentation of Risk:** By moving toward "Association Plans" and vouchers, we risk a **market death spiral.** Healthy individuals will opt for low-cost, "junk" plans, while the sickest patients--those requiring the most intensive wound care and surgical intervention--will see their premiums skyrocket as the risk pool dissolves.
* **The Uninsured Surge:** Projections suggest that dismantling the ACA's subsidy structure could lead to **4 million people** losing coverage almost instantly. For a private practice, this translates to more uncompensated care and more patients presenting to the ER with complications that could have been managed in-office.

* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=186014565&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg2MDE0NTY1LCJpYXQiOjE3Njk1NTY5ODcsImV4cCI6MTc3MjE0ODk4NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Mqeu4ezuPrEKe7vh7IA2BdVJwr1Fum2woHJQ5-LjHz0)
* * *
**Why This Won 't Work for Americans (or Their Doctors)**
This plan fails because it ignores the **administrative reality of the physician.**
1\. **Increased Physician Burden:** If we move to a voucher-based system, the burden of verifying eligibility and managing payments shifts further onto the practice. We are already drowning in documentation; we don't need to become HSA administrators too.
2\. **Lack of Protective Teeth:** The proposal is dangerously thin on how it will protect those with pre-existing conditions once the ACA's foundational market rules are scrapped. "Concepts" don't pay for skin substitutes or surgical suites.
3\. **Fiscal Instability:** While the administration claims a $36 billion savings by cutting "insurance kickbacks," the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget warns this model could balloon the deficit by **$350 billion**. We've seen this movie before: when the deficit grows, reimbursement rates are the first thing on the chopping block.
**Final Thoughts**
We need a system that prioritizes clinical outcomes over insurance company profiteering. While I applaud the focus on transparency and PBM reform, "The Great Healthcare Plan" feels more like a financial experiment than a medical solution. We don't need more "concepts." We need a stable, evidence-based policy that allows us to do what we were trained to do: **treat patients.**

A physician explains why Trump's proposal risks patients, doctors, and the stability of American medicine | | and | Jan 27 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. On January 15, the Trump administration unveiled what it grandly labeled" The Great Healthcare Plan," a proposal that promises lower costs, greater transparency, and more "consumer choice" in American healthcare. Strip away the branding, however, and the plan amounts to a familiar Trump-era formula: deregulation wrapped in slogans, thin on specifics, heavy on disruption. The proposal emphasizes insurer and hospital transparency, targets pharmacy benefit managers, and replaces traditional insurance subsidies with individual healthcare vouchers and expanded Health Savings Accounts. What it notably fails to do is explain--at a policy, clinical, or operational level--how seriously ill patients are supposed to navigate this system, how risk pools remain stable, or how physicians already drowning in administrative work are expected to absorb yet another layer of complexity. As with so many Trump initiatives, the plan gestures toward reform while outsourcing the consequences to patients and frontline providers. What follows is a physician's view from inside that reality. Dr., wrote this article and Blue Amp Media is publishing it here with permission. by Dr. Eric Lullove For those of us in the trenches of private practice--navigating the labyrinth of Medicare LCDs, fighting the "death by a thousand cuts" of prior authorizations, and watching administrative bloat swallow clinical outcomes--the latest healthcare proposal from the Trump administration feels like a case of d eja vu. They're calling it " The Great Healthcare Plan." But as a physician who spends as much time reviewing reimbursement policy as I do treating complex wounds and complex patients, I have to ask: Where is the actual healthcare in this plan? What we've been presented with isn't a blueprint for clinical excellence or system-wide stability. It's a deregulatory framework disguised as "consumer choice," and it risks leaving both patients and providers in a precarious position. The Anatomy of the Proposal The administration's January 15 rollout centers on four primary pillars. On the surface, some of these sound like the common-sense reforms we've been advocating for in the wound care and medical communities: Transparency over Profiteering: The "Plain English" standard for insurers and hospitals is a move toward exposing the opaque "spread pricing" that keeps patients in the dark. Targeting the Middlemen: There is a renewed focus on Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) and broker kickbacks--the administrative parasites that inflate costs without adding a single gram of clinical value. The Voucher Pivot: This is the most radical shift. The plan effectively ends direct subsidies to insurance companies, instead funneling that capital directly into Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) or "Healthcare Vouchers" for individuals. The Pros: Shining a Light on the "Black Box" There are elements here that make sense. Price transparency is long overdue. If we are forced to justify every CPT code and CTP application with mountain-high documentation, it is only fair that hospitals and insurers are forced to show their hand regarding profit margins and denial rates. Furthermore, the $50 billion commitment to Rural Healthcare --leveraging the Working Families Tax Cuts Act --is a necessary acknowledgement that our rural infrastructure is on life support. Investing in tech and facility modernization is a win for access, provided the money actually reaches the bedside. The Cons: The Administrative Burden and the "Death Spiral" Here is where the clinical reality clashes with the political "concept." As someone who understands the intricacies of the CMS fee schedule, I see several red flags: The "Consumer" Fallacy: The plan treats healthcare like a retail commodity. Expecting a patient with a chronic limb-threatening ischemia or a complex wound or even having a heart attack or stroke to "shop around" with a voucher is not just unrealistic; it's dangerous. Healthcare isn't a luxury watch or a high-end espresso machine; it is a necessity that often requires immediate, expert intervention. Fragmentation of Risk: By moving toward "Association Plans" and vouchers, we risk a market death spiral. Healthy individuals will opt for low-cost, "junk" plans, while the sickest patients--those requiring the most intensive wound care and surgical intervention--will see their premiums skyrocket as the risk pool dissolves. The Uninsured Surge: Projections suggest that dismantling the ACA's subsidy structure could lead to 4 million people losing coverage almost instantly. For a private practice, this translates to more uncompensated care and more patients presenting to the ER with complications that could have been managed in-office. Why This Won 't Work for Americans (or Their Doctors) This plan fails because it ignores the administrative reality of the physician. 1\. Increased Physician Burden: If we move to a voucher-based system, the burden of verifying eligibility and managing payments shifts further onto the practice. We are already drowning in documentation; we don't need to become HSA administrators too. 2\. Lack of Protective Teeth: The proposal is dangerously thin on how it will protect those with pre-existing conditions once the ACA's foundational market rules are scrapped. "Concepts" don't pay for skin substitutes or surgical suites. 3\. Fiscal Instability: While the administration claims a $36 billion savings by cutting "insurance kickbacks," the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget warns this model could balloon the deficit by $350 billion. We've seen this movie before: when the deficit grows, reimbursement rates are the first thing on the chopping block. Final Thoughts We need a system that prioritizes clinical outcomes over insurance company profiteering. While I applaud the focus on transparency and PBM reform, "The Great Healthcare Plan" feels more like a financial experiment than a medical solution. We don't need more "concepts." We need a stable, evidence-based policy that allows us to do what we were trained to do: treat patients. | | ---|---|--- READ MORE BLUE AMP MEDIA | | and | | ---|---|--- | Jan 26 | | | and | | ---|---|--- | Jan 25 | * | A guest post by| . subject: A new chapter in American health
body:
The case for protein, strength, and long-term resilience | Friends,

America is entering a new chapter in how we think about food and health.

With the release of the new federal nutrition guidelines, there’s growing recognition that the old model of counting calories, fearing protein, and chasing food trends has failed too many people.

What’s been missing from this conversation is muscle.

**Muscle isn’t just about strength or appearance. It’s the foundation of metabolic health, resilience as we age, and long-term independence.** And yet for decades, it’s been overlooked in our national approach to nutrition and wellness.

_That’s why I wrote The Forever Strong Playbook._

[ ](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=743e721e60b14f60bd0fa97a8c1bb048&_e=LQjyxxbz7L0k3BqUszSc5P3vKyOMmrSVCw-lw2UPcQwxXBWjJ6cyt3wSBbbZnBr13IlhGTQCl8YjBLQtjTzaB9CjqgYzgrwmbm-TN6v0IjRpA8C6ww8mBSj9z129WuTLupLZpxeHDU90Jg8AYUPNOy6XlQ-6qZ2L0h2Iw7xUoc4N5wQrkU8iolBPvl1-GqoNcMll7IdaJhNOZ8sTM3pzW3S490ny9ZgrsrE7iHdnAcJ15-FOcYTfyy6waKnVms0Re2iihZQSxLBO9Xm4-HcQTU9Td6ZwJHGen7uChPNLRXLvIUDX1EMxJQOAmlhyBqcYqd9aPoJlgoXD9MPca-AgPwf4-uyeiPw1Mwampb8zI4w%3D)

Democrats are NOT going to allow this to go unanswered next year. Will you help change the momentum? I am not asking for millions of dollars, nor even $100 (but if you can spare it, I would appreciate it). Last cycle, I was the architect of our new Senate majority. That's put a #1 target on my back. body:
Gina Hinojosa is the leader Texas needs — and I know she has what it takes to beat Greg Abbott.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter,
Ruben Gallego here, U.S. Senator from Arizona.
As someone who’s done it,**I know what it takes to win a tough race.** Or better yet, I know who it takes — and my friend Gina Hinojosa has what it takes to beat Greg Abbott and become the next Governor of Texas.
But Gina can’t do this without our support. **[I’ll do my part on the campaign trail, and I’d love it if you could step up with a donation today!](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260127_1_gallegosurrogate.mi-su8&refcode=em20260127-485&t=1&akid=485%2E299639%2E0bhDc7)**
Gina is a Texas state representative, attorney, advocate, and mom of two boys who has spent her career challenging the status quo, taking on corrupt politicians, and putting Texas families first.
Now, Gina’s running for Governor because Texans deserve better than Greg Abbott, a corrupt politician who puts billionaire campaign donors ahead of families. He’s gutted public schools, dismantled basic freedoms, and made the rich even richer while leaving working people further behind every step of the way.
But here’s the thing:**Greg Abbott has never been this vulnerable before.** On issue after issue, he’s underwater with voters across party lines. After a decade of Abbott’s corruption, voters are exhausted and ready for a change — and Gina’s the leader Texas needs to deliver it.
Gina has been fighting Abbott in the state legislature for nearly a decade on public school funding, flood relief, gerrymandering, and so much more.**She knows how to take him on — and he knows it, too.** That’s why he wasted no time attacking her after she launched her campaign.
That’s where we come in, Peter. Abbott has his billionaire donors, but Gina has us. Our early support is crucial to ensuring Gina can compete at the scale this race demands and make sure voters hear her message — _not_ Abbott’s misinformation.
[**Will you pitch in $15 right now to help Gina build a campaign strong enough to not only fight back against Abbott’s attacks, but _defeat_ him this fall?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20260127_1_gallegosurrogate.QUZlu7&refcode=em20260127-485&t=2&akid=485%2E299639%2E0bhDc7)

Thanks for your support. Let’s do this!
Ruben Gallego

name: Theresa Flores
subject: Friend, I was trafficked at 15
body:
I survived child trafficking. Many children don’t—unless someone acts.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e14976522/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvU2VqNE5zWEh3WA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMjc/LbmNsR0xkU0Q1Qg/qP2hpZHM9bmNRb0xTVzN4c1lNOGVscw/gaXlIog/sat243d8204)
| |
---
| |
---
| GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | Friend,

I am a survivor of child trafficking—and today, I work to make sure other children never face what I did. My name is Theresa Flores. **I was fifteen years old.** **An honor student.
****A daughter.
****A girl who trusted the wrong "friend.”** I was trafficked for two years. Most people imagine trafficking happens far away - in dark alleys or foreign countries. **To “other people.”** But my nightmare happened in the suburbs of Detroit. I lived at home.
I went to high school.
**And no one noticed.** On the worst night of my life, I was taken to a dirty motel room and auctioned off to nearly two dozen men. **I remember the smell of the room.
****The fear in my chest.
****And the silence I was forced to keep.** I survived. But many do not.
---
[ Help Save a Child ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
That’s why I partner with the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** Through education and intervention, they equip frontline partners to do what most systems never taught— _help ordinary people to recognize trafficking before it’s too late._ Partners supported by **Sound of Freedom Foundation** train hotel employees—men and women working in places like the motel I was taken to — to see what they were never taught to look for. **To notice what others miss.
****And to report it.** This is how **prevention becomes possible**. Because one informed employee and one brave phone call can save a life. **Here's the truth most people don’t know.** The majority of trafficking in America happens in hotels and motels. And it spikes around large sports events, conventions and concerts - anywhere demand increases. **There’s more you should know.**
---
* Human trafficking is the second-largest criminal enterprise in the world.
* **In the United States alone, 9 out of 10 missing children are trafficked.**
* If a child is not found within 48 hours, the risk of trafficking skyrockets.
* The average age of a trafficked child is 12 to 14 years old.

---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**These are children.** Not criminals.
Not “prostitutes.” **Children.** **I ask you urgently - please pray they'll be found.**
---
[ Help Save a Child ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**Sound of Freedom Foundation** partners don’t stop at rescue. They help care for survivors too. Across the country, partners host healing events and wellness weekends—safe places where survivors can rest, connect, and begin again. Survivors are offered opportunities to learn self-defense, engage in therapeutic art and movement, and build practical life skills. Sessions help survivors learn forgiveness, rebuild trust, form healthy relationships, and set strong boundaries. **How we care for survivors matters just as much as rescuing them.** You are hearing from me today because the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** helps make this work possible. And because children are worth fighting for. I want you to know this: **Your support is not abstract.
****It reaches motel rooms and f****rightened children - in moments****when seconds matter.** It reaches places I once stood— without help. **Today, by the grace of God, I am a survivor.** An advocate. And the author so others can recognize the signs sooner. **But my story is not the point.
****The children who are still trapped are.**
---
[ Help Save a Child ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Every outreach is a race against time.
Every trained volunteer is a shield. And **YOU** can be part of the rescue. Whether you give once or stand with the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** through steady, monthly support - your generosity saves lives - quietly, consistently and courageously. **YOU can help save children from harm.** **We would be deeply grateful.** **THANK YOU.** You are helping rewrite endings.
You are helping children believe freedom is possible.
---
For God's Children,
---
Theresa Flores
Freedom Fighter
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ **Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074
---

# An Economy That Works for All
# Not Just the Billionaires!

Friends,
I need your help! An economy that works for all is not a radical idea. It is the bare minimum.
* It means the right to safe, affordable housing.
* It means universal healthcare.
* It means universal childcare, 3-K, and pre-K.
* It means clean air, clean water, reliable energy, and healthy, safe communities.
* It means wages you can live on and an economy that rewards work, not wealth hoarding!

This is what we are fighting for in Ohio. And this is exactly why powerful interests are working overtime to protect a system that works for them and them alone.
We are heading into a critical moment.[ **Our January 31 fundraising deadline is approaching** ,**and what we raise now determines how strong we enter the primary season. Not later. Not in the spring. Now.**](https://tristanrader.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe296f262404fb3f98dc9e04f&id=f5c8f1a97f&e=869bcf0641)
[**Give Today!!**](https://tristanrader.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe296f262404fb3f98dc9e04f&id=4bc0c26911&e=869bcf0641)
If we are serious about building an Ohio that works for everyone, this is the moment to invest in it.
**Chip in before January 31** to power a grassroots campaign that is actually building something better.
[**$10 helps.
$25 matters.**](https://tristanrader.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe296f262404fb3f98dc9e04f&id=2b5ad5c904&e=869bcf0641)
Whatever you can give makes a real difference.
This campaign is not powered by corporate donors or billionaire money. It is powered by people who believe the basics should not be luxuries.
And we would love to see you in person as we build this movement together.
[**Join us for our February Campaign Fundraiser**](https://tristanrader.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe296f262404fb3f98dc9e04f&id=3987dfa8b2&e=869bcf0641)
**Friday, February 27th**
**5:00 PM to 8:00 PM**
**One Star Bar**
14048 Detroit Ave.
Lakewood, OH 44107
Everyone is welcome. No one will be turned away for inability to pay. Come build community, share space, and help strengthen a movement that is about more than politics. It is about the future we are building together.
We are not asking for too much.
We are asking for what every person deserves.
Let’s build it together.
In solidarity,
**Tristan Rader**
State Representative

I’m an immigrant, Peter. I’m also a human being — and an American. The chaos and violence that ICE has brought into our cities this past year needs to stop, and it needs to stop _immediately._ We’ve witnessed them kidnap people off the streets, terrorize entire communities, rip babies away from their parents — and in recent weeks, kill two innocent Americans in broad daylight. No one, regardless of their immigration status or the color of their skin, should be forced to suffer at the hands of an ICE agency that’s sowing fear into our communities and acting with zero accountability. Republicans want to give ICE and DHS a blank check to continue terrorizing this country, but this lawlessness cannot be allowed to continue. **That’s why I will vote against their budget bill that hands ICE even more of our taxpayer dollars and continue to fight to ensure that the agency faces real accountability.** Thank you, Mazie

Hey folks,
I went solo in the studio. No guest, no script. Just me, the chat, and a whole lot of very real anger, fear, and clarity about where we are right now. We talked about ICE, the murder of Alex Pretti, the White House's panicked PR cleanup, and why Democrats finally have the leverage -- _if_ they're willing to use it. We also got deep into the politics, the messaging traps, and the bigger question a lot of people are afraid to say out loud: what happens if this keeps getting worse?
**Here 's what I got into:**

— advancing nominees who have no business serving on the federal bench.

It’s literally a documented pattern.

Over and over again, Senate Democrats have allowed Trump-aligned judges
with extreme records, open hostility to civil rights, and strict loyalty
to Trump’s agenda to move forward. Judges who were rushed through
hearings, waved past red flags, and handed lifetime appointments anyway.

Once confirmed, these judges are untouchable. And February’s hearings will
determine whether this cycle continues.

Will Senate Democrats finally break with their own history and stop
advancing judges who exist solely to entrench Trumpism in our courts? Or
will they once again allow “process,” “norms,” and political convenience
to override what’s right?

Hi Peter,

Someone asked me a question at a recent town hall that stuck with me:

“What separates you from another Democrat in the race who eventually
called what’s happening in Gaza a genocide?”

It’s a fair question, and I want to give you my honest explanation.

First, imagine someone asks you what color the sky is. You’d immediately
say blue.

Now, picture someone else who doesn’t answer the question clearly. They
stall. They wait to see what everyone else says.

Months go by before they finally admit, “Fine... it’s blue,” but only after
checking if that answer was okay to say.

Clearly, something is odd about that. And what if you later learned the
reason they hesitated to call the sky blue was because they were trying to
win over support from people who didn’t want them to say blue?

That’s the difference between me and the other candidate,
Peter.

I don’t gut-check my beliefs with AIPAC or any pro-Israel groups behind
closed doors.

I’ve been honest about my stance on this from day one: Our tax dollars
shouldn’t fund genocide overseas. They should be invested in improving
life here at home.

This will undoubtedly make me enemy #1 in AIPAC’s eyes, and honestly,
that’s fine with me.

I’m not running for Senate to appease AIPAC or any billionaire-backed
group. I’m running to fight for working people.

clean_body: Why Charlie stepped away — one day a week| | | | | Peter, | | Charlie Kirk built a movement for truth -- but his final message pointed to something eternal. It wasn't about politics... or elections... or even about the culture war. His final book was deeply personal, and unlike anything Charlie had written before... It was about the Sabbath. About sacred rest. Reconnecting with God. Charlie wrote this book because he knew what America was missing... and what he nearly lost himself. He found that in a world addicted to busyness, noise, and scrolling... The most radical act of resistance is to STOP. To rest. To reflect. To return to God. This book is his blueprint for how we do that -- as individuals, as families, and as a nation. 🔥 You'll discover how Charlie learned to honor the Sabbath in a culture that never stops 🔥 How setting aside just one day a week gave him clarity, peace, and strength 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark a spiritual revival across America I know he would've wanted you to have this book. When you give today to Turning Point USA, you 're not just supporting the movement Charlie built -- you're helping pass on the message he felt most urgently in his final months. Peter, thank you, in advance, for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage -- the very things Charlie gave his life for. And as you do, may the message of this book lead you -- just as it led Charlie -- to a deeper trust in God, a stronger love for your family, and a renewed peace in your own soul. For Charlie, Justin Streiff Chief Operating Officer Turning Point USA P.S. Charlie Kirk's final book, Stop, in the Name of God, is a heartfelt call to slow down, remember what's eternal, and rest in God. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

Fellow American, I'll keep this note brief and to the point because we don't have much time left. **_With the end-of-month deadline rapidly approaching, we 're in grave danger of _MISSING_ our January fundraising goal! _** I wish I could say I was surprised... But this is just another example of the trends we've been seeing for the last few months. Right now, far too many Republicans are sitting on the sidelines. _We 're seeing it in elections, we're seeing it in our voter verification numbers, we're seeing it in our fundraising, and frankly, _we 're even seeing it in the number of conservatives reading our emails_!_ _ _ But you're among the few % who opened. And I'm not surprised, because your record shows you're a top supporter, so you're among the few I can count on to read this email from start to finish, ${Recipient.FirstName}. **To be fully transparent - I don't have any checks left to cash or large pledges. Unlike the Democrats, I don't have left-wing mega-donors I can call up to bankroll our grassroots campaign. ** At this make-or-break moment, grassroots supporters like _YOU_ are _truly_ the last place left for me to turn. Fellow American, you've always had my back when I needed it most. With time running out, I have no choice but to ask for your support one final time. _(I understand that things are still tough as we recover from four years of Biden 's economy. body:
We need justice for Louisiana’s coastlines, not evasion from Chevron. | |
---
Peter, **Multi-billion dollar polluter company Chevron is playing games with our justice system.** Chevron stands accused of violating coastal restoration law in Louisiana, having broken the terms of or failing to obtain necessary permits. Louisiana’s Solicitor General says Chevron doesn’t deny that “they dumped billions of gallons” of oil and gas extraction byproduct “directly into our marsh."1 **But Chevron knows it’s more likely to have a more sympathetic ear in the federal court system than in the state of Louisiana, so it’s trying to get the case moved.** The stakes are high for both Chevron and the Bayou State—last year a Louisiana jury found that Chevron owed one Louisiana parish $744.6 million. That could make a huge difference for the restoration of Louisiana’s coastline -- but Chevron would rather use that money to enrich their wealthy shareholders. A 21-year-old New Braunfels woman **[faces arson and burglary charges](https://substack.com/redirect/57594246-fd61-4212-8af0-c519a2e94ff2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after allegedly breaking into the Comal County Republican Party headquarters on January 14, starting a small fire, and causing minor damage--no injuries reported, authorities said.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/57594246-fd61-4212-8af0-c519a2e94ff2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Suspect Quickly Apprehended** Grace Carol Brown, 21, arrested January 22 without incident after joint probe by local police, fire marshal, and FBI; bond set at $200,000 combined.
* **Incident Details Emerge** On January 14, employees found broken window and small fire at Comal County GOP office in New Braunfels; damage was limited and no one harmed.
* **Officials Condemn Trend** Texas GOP chair calls attack troubling amid rising vandalism against Republican offices nationwide; RNC chair blames inflammatory rhetoric for inciting violence.

* * *
# Never-Trumper Wilson demands Stephen Miller hang
Never-Trumper Rick Wilson **[unleashed a profane tirade on the Lincoln Project podcast,](https://substack.com/redirect/4da9134c-24d1-43c7-bdc3-bc0423314a2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** calling for top Trump aide Stephen Miller to face Nuremberg-style trials and execution over immigration enforcement policies.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4da9134c-24d1-43c7-bdc3-bc0423314a2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Wilson Likens Miller** to Nazi criminal, branding him architect of "ICE-stapo" operations in DHS and demanding he be first to "tried and convicted and f*cking dangles" at future trials.
* **Comments Tied To** recent anti-ICE protester shooting, where Wilson blasted Miller for labeling the deceased a domestic terrorist despite his clean record and nursing background.
* **Wilson 's History** includes repeated inflammatory rhetoric, from suggesting bullets for Trump in 2015 to labeling him fascist traitor in 2024 amid ongoing anti-MAGA campaigns.

body:
Rents are up more than 40 percent since 2020, statewide in California. The price of a home in Los Angeles has climbed 43.6 percent over that same period. Groceries cost 23.6 percent more than they did just four years ago.

| | |
---
Hi Peter, Rents are up more than **40 percent** since 2020, statewide in California. The price of a home in Los Angeles has climbed **43.6 percent** over that same period. Groceries cost **23.6 percent more** than they did just four years ago. For millions of families, these facts mean daily, painful trade-offs. Pay the rent - or buy enough food.
Cover groceries - or fall behind on utilities.
Keep up with the bills - and forget ever being able to save enough for a down payment on a home. Most people agree America is facing a terrible affordability crisis. Who has a plan to fix it? Last week in Los Angeles, voters heard from a candidate who does. **Rob Lucero Debates the Socialists** At the **South Asian Network candidates’ forum** for California’s 34th Congressional District in Los Angeles, several candidates spoke about the rising cost of living. Incumbent Jimmy Gomez didn't bother to show up. The Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) candidates promised various “free” services if elected. But when it came time to explain how those promises would actually be paid for, the answers never went much further than a familiar slogan: _tax the rich_. Rob Lucero took a very different approach. **Why Has the Standard of Living Gone Down for So Many?** Inflation is caused by “too many dollars chasing too few goods.” So, let’s increase the amount of goods being produced! Instead of resigning ourselves to being a pitiful “service economy”, let’s **revive manufacturing** and return to being a producing nation. We can massively increase the number of houses available, and create tens of millions of new, well-paid jobs with a **REAL New Deal** , the way FDR got the USA out of the Terrible Depression. **How to Finance an Economic Recovery?** The key to financing such a gigantic and transformative plan is contained in HR 5356, the National Infrastructure Bank Act of 2025. This new federally created bank would make **$5 trillion in credit available to invest in large-scale infrastructure projects** that would employ **25 million nationwide** , and **one million in California** , rebuilding the country. Rob’s plan includes the **American System Corps** , a national public works and service program to put Americans back to work rebuilding our bridges, water systems, expanding our power production, producing affordable housing, and restoring the industries that make our communities strong. The American System Corps would create good-paying jobs, expand apprenticeship programs, and give young people a pathway to meaningful careers — all while tackling the root causes of inflation and scarcity. **Learn More and Take Action** Rob has a 3.5 minute video about the American System Corps and a petition you can sign if it makes sense to you: [https://www.luceroforcongress.com/american_system_corps_petition](https://www.luceroforcongress.com/american_system_corps_petition?e=39cdcb2fb7adda80e7fc66430579bb85&utm_source=luceroforcongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=san_forum_affordability&n=1) The next 34th district Congressional Candidate’s forum will be hosted by the American Legion Eagle Rock Post 276 on March 11th. Put the date on your calendar. Rob will be there. During the week of March 11th, Congressmen are assigned to return to their districts. Jimmy Gomez has no excuse not to show up at this next Candidate's Forum. America has a real chance at an exciting future. Join Rob’s campaign and get involved to make a difference.
**Team Lucero**
**Rob Lucero****
**Candidate for U.S. Congress – CA-34
“Country before party. People before politics.” info@luceroforcongress.com
[https://www.luceroforcongress.com/](https://www.luceroforcongress.com/?e=39cdcb2fb7adda80e7fc66430579bb85&utm_source=luceroforcongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=san_forum_affordability&n=2)
---

name: Beto O'Rourke (via LeftNet)
subject: Hope is showing up all over Texas
body:
I’ve been on the road recruiting the people who will be on the ballot – and it’s working.
#
To do my part so that we win the 2026 midterms, I’ve been on the road across Texas recruiting the people who will actually be on the ballot. I want to tell you a little bit about it if you’ve got a minute.
In Fort Worth, in Tarrant County – one of the last truly competitive big counties in our state – I stood in a packed room in a local brewery and asked a simple question:
_Who here is willing to run?_
Sixteen people raised their hands.
The next day in Collin County, another tough, fast-growing, swing region, 22 more Texans said yes. And in places Republicans assume we’ve written off – Waco, Brazos County, rural communities – hundreds more showed up to say they’re ready to fight.
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22175?t=1&akid=1481%2E2118727%2E47mUh7)
Here’s why this matters:
When Democrats are on every place on the ballot – from county commissioner to Congress – we don’t just win more races. We register more voters. We turn out more neighbors. We build power that lasts.
That’s how we won Tarrant County in 2018. That’s how we got within striking distance statewide.
And that’s how we take back Texas in 2026.
Right now, people all over Texas are stepping forward. They’re choosing action over despair. Hope over resignation.
I need you with us.
**[We’re organizing everywhere in Texas, all year round. Add your name today to be part of Powered by People’s growing movement.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22175?t=2&akid=1481%2E2118727%2E47mUh7)**
**[ADD YOUR NAME ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22175?t=3&akid=1481%2E2118727%2E47mUh7)**
We’re showing up, fighting on every front, for every position on the ballot, conceding nothing and working until we win.
[**Democrats are running for every seat on the ballot in 2026. Now, we need to help them win. Add your name today to join Powered by People’s fight for the future of Texas.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22175?t=4&akid=1481%2E2118727%2E47mUh7)
Thank you.
Beto O’Rourke

**LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.**
